Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported in connection with this Form 1099-R (writable)
Fact.Description:
THE FORM 1099-R LEG of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13: "Enter the total of any amounts reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain' on a Schedule K-1, Form 1099-DIV, or Form 2439 from an estate, a trust, a real estate investment trust, or a mutual fund (or other regulated investment company) **or in connection with a Form 1099-R**". Before this fill that leg entered the worksheet as a literal <Dollar>0</Dollar> in scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13, and the reason recorded there was that /form1099Rs existed as a collection but carried no unrecaptured section 1250 amount — a missing collection FIELD, which is what this fact is.
PER FORM, NOT PER RETURN, and that is the one place this leg differs from its three siblings. The Form 2439 and estate/trust Schedule K-1 legs are attested return-level TOTALS because this dictionary models neither notice; /form1099Rs IS modeled, item by item, so the amount attaches to the form that reported it exactly as the Form 1099-DIV box 2b leg attaches to /dividendReports/*. The worksheet still receives one total — /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm1099Rs sums the items — so the printed line is answered by a total either way.
NO BOX NUMBER IS CLAIMED, deliberately, and this is the sharp edge of the leg. The worksheet line names the FORM and not a box, unlike its Form 1099-DIV sibling ("box 2b") and unlike the Form 2439 leg, which the same instructions route to box 1b at :508-512. Nothing in the vendored corpus ties this amount to a numbered box of Form 1099-R, so this intake does not say it is a component of box 3 (capital gain) or of any other box, and no upper bound is derived from one.
A CONSEQUENCE OF THAT SILENCE WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN GUESSING: if the amount were always inside box 3, this leg would be knockout-coupled — /flowKnockoutRetirementCapitalGain refuses any return with a box-3 capital gain above $0, so no filer could reach it. The vendored sources do not say so, and this fill does not assume it; the honest statement is that the reachable population is a filer with such an amount and a blank box 3, and that whether that population is empty is an OPEN question, recorded in form1099Rs_memory.json rather than resolved by assertion.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents. MIN $0 on the line's own wording — it asks for "amounts reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 GAIN'", with no loss branch, the same rule the box-2b twin /dividendReports/*/writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain and the Form 2439 leg carry. No Round here; the worksheet's single Round sits at /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm1099Rs and the worksheet's own floor at scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250Gain. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias ../unrecapturedSection1250Gain downstream.

The complete-safe alias of ../writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain: the answered amount when answered, $0 otherwise. THE IsComplete/Switch IDIOM, never a bare Placeholder — a blank field on one Form 1099-R must not make the sum below Incomplete, which is the failure this repo has paid for three times. Deliberately UNLIKE the box-3 sibling ../capitalGain, which keeps itself Incomplete when blank so the MeF export can tell "the filer entered $0" from "the filer entered nothing"; this fact has no export of its own and exists only to be summed, so an unanswered field is $0.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported in connection with Form(s) 1099-R
Fact.Description:
The total across every Form 1099-R on the return — the FORM 1099-R LEG of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13), the last of that line's four legs to become real. The other three shipped earlier: /dividendReports /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromDividends (Form 1099-DIV box 2b), scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 (box 1b, attested) and scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 (the estate-or-trust K-1 total, attested). With this fact, scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13 carries no <Dollar>0</Dollar> leg at all.
COMPLETE-SAFE, AND THE GUARD IS THE POINT. The IsComplete wrapper around /form1099Rs is the landmine this repo has paid for three times: a CollectionSum over an UNANSWERED collection does not resolve, and this fact is consumed by a worksheet that must stay Complete on every return that has no Form 1099-R section at all. Wrapped, the Switch short-circuits to $0 and every pre-existing scenario is byte-identical. The per-item alias carries the second half of the same guard: a Form 1099-R present with this field blank contributes $0 rather than poisoning the sum.
ROUNDING: the single Round of this leg sits here, matching the box-2b sibling. The worksheet's own floor is line 18's, applied once at scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250Gain, and is deliberately not duplicated.
DIRECTION OF THE MOVEMENT THIS FILL CAUSES: strictly UPWARD on line 13, therefore on Schedule D line 19, therefore on the 25%-rate group of the Schedule D Tax Worksheet and of Form 6251 Part III. The defect it closes was taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and silent — the slice was short and the gain fell to the long-term rate. It moves no return that does not answer the new field.

Fact.Description:

THE NON-ELECTING FILER IS NOT REFUSED, on Form 4972's own item 1: "If you don't use Form 4972 ... Report the entire amount from box 1 (Gross distribution) of Form 1099-R on line 5a, and the taxable amount on line 5b." THE IRA FORM IS OUT OF THIS GUARD ENTIRELY (../notIraSepSimple), and that carve-out is the second half of the correction. Fact.Description:
The three printed line-4c boxes plus the "no election" state. "rollover" is box 1 and selects Exception 1; "qcd" is box 2 and selects Exception 3; "hfd" is box 3, whose label the filer writes by hand, and selects Exception 4. "none" is not a box: it is the ordinary case in which no Exception applies and box 2a is the taxable amount.
BOX 3 CARRIES TWO DIFFERENT ELECTIONS, which this vocabulary does not distinguish and which the sentence above therefore under-states (found by reading Pub 590-B rather than the Form 1040 instructions). The instructions label box 3 HFD and have the filer write "HFD" beside it; Pub 590-B sends the ONE-TIME QCD to a split-interest entity to the SAME box with "SIE" written beside it instead. So "hfd" is really "box 3", and a fill on that box owes both elections a disposition. The mirror-image hazard - an SIE distribution arriving under "qcd", because a filer choosing among four LABELS rather than box numbers will read a QCD to a charitable remainder trust as a QCD - is closed by ../writableIsQcdToSplitInterestEntity, which refuses it. The HFD fill closed the hazard on the other side too, with ../writableIsBox3SplitInterestEntityQcd, so both labels now refuse an SIE election and the box is symmetric.
MORE THAN ONE BOX CAN BE CHECKED ON ONE DISTRIBUTION, and this vocabulary carries them in three slots rather than as a multi-select. The instructions say that if more than one Exception applies the filer checks a box for each and includes a statement showing the amount of each ("Line 4b - $1,000 Rollover and $500 HFD"); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 28. A single-valued Enum cannot carry two boxes, so the second and third boxes are their own writables over these same four options, ../writableLine4cSecondElection and ../writableLine4cThirdElection, read complete-safe through ../line4cSecondElection and ../line4cThirdElection. THREE SLOTS SATURATE THE PRINTED ROW: line 4c prints exactly three boxes, so a fourth slot would not be expressible on the form. "Box 2 is checked" and "box 3 is checked" are then single facts spanning every slot - ../hasQcdElection and ../hasHfdElection - and ../line4bTaxableAmount's two subtrahends CAN both be positive on one form. THE ONLY SUPPORTED COMBINATION BEYOND A SINGLE BOX IS QCD PLUS HFD: every other two-box combination, the same option twice included, fails ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection's pair Case, and a THIRD answered slot is refused outright by the Case above it, since every triple contains a rollover beside an exclusion. Both are refused through ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution and /knockoutIraSepSimple. The statement itself is an attachment, and what this dictionary lacks is a FREE-TEXT attachment idiom, not an attachment idiom as such: the BOOLEAN one exists and works, /writableForm5329Line54ReasonableCauseStatementAttached feeding /form5329Line54WaiverRequiresReasonableCauseStatement, with Schedule F and Form 4835 on the same shape. That pair is the precedent a successor should follow here; what is missing is attachment PROSE, and inventing a free-text surface for line 4c alone is what this module will not do.
WHY THIS CARRIES AN Export WHEN NO OTHER EnumOptions FACT IN THIS DICTIONARY DOES. It has three real consumers - ../writableLine4cElection's Writable declaration and the Enum literals inside ../line4cElection and ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection - but every one of them reads it through the optionsPath ATTRIBUTE, and the facts manifest's depends_on edge set models element dependencies only, so all three edges are invisible to scripts/lint_wiring.py. The Export states the fact that the edge model drops. The other 63 EnumOptions facts do not need it: 60 are inherited from the frozen ty2024-l0 vendoring and exempt for that reason, 2 are genuinely consumed through EnumOptionsSize expressions, and the last predates the wiring lint's shrink-only rule for its exemption list.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4c - the election this Form 1099-R cannot show
Fact.Description:
User response: which line-4c box the filer checks for this IRA distribution. A Form 1099-R cannot carry this answer. The custodian does not know that a distribution was rolled over, given to charity or moved into an HSA, so on a FULL rollover reported without a rollover code, a full QCD or a full HFD the form is indistinguishable from an ordinary fully-taxable distribution and box 2a equals box 1. The election lives only with the filer and on line 4c, which is why it is a writable rather than a derived fact.
PER ITEM, not per return, because the Exceptions apply distribution by distribution: a filer may roll one IRA distribution over and take another in cash. Line 4c itself is a single row of checkboxes on the return, which the aggregation of these per-item answers determines: /anyLine4cRolloverElection, /anyLine4cQcdElection and /anyLine4cHfdElection are those aggregations, and they are what the printed row is bound to.
THE FIRST OF THREE SLOTS. A distribution to which two Exceptions apply checks two boxes; the second answer is ../writableLine4cSecondElection, over the same four options, and the supported pair is a QCD in one slot and an HFD in the other. A third box is ../writableLine4cThirdElection, which is refused whenever it is answered because no triple computes. Ask this one first; a lone exception always belongs here.
NOT ASKED for a form whose IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is unchecked: line 4c belongs to line 4, the IRA line. A pension or annuity distribution has its OWN rollover/PSO checkbox on line 5c, which is a different vocabulary and is not modeled here. ../line4cElection enforces that by resolving "none" on any non-IRA form even if this writable is somehow answered.

Fact.Name: The line 4c election in force for this Form 1099-R
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of ../writableLine4cElection. Resolves the "none" option in the two states that must behave identically to the pre-election dictionary: the writable is unanswered, or the form is not IRA-flagged (line 4c is line 4's checkbox; a pension form's own election lives on line 5c and is out of this unit). Never Incomplete, so every consumer can read it without an IsComplete wrapper of its own.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4c - a SECOND box checked for this Form 1099-R
Fact.Description: ASK: "Does a second line 4c exception also apply to this IRA distribution?" and, if so, which one. HELP: line 4c is a row of checkboxes, and the printed instruction says that if more than one exception applies you check a box for each and attach a statement showing the amount of each ("Line 4b - $1,000 Rollover and $500 HFD"); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 28. ASKED WHEN: the form's IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked AND ../writableLine4cElection is already answered with something other than "none" - a lone exception belongs in the first slot, never here. UNANSWERED: no second exception; the form behaves exactly as it did before this slot existed, and nothing is Incomplete. VALIDATION: the same four options as the first slot (none, rollover, qcd, hfd); the ONLY combination this dictionary can compute is a QCD in one slot and an HFD in the other, and every other pairing - including the same option twice - is refused by ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection through ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution and /knockoutIraSepSimple, so the application should offer only the option the first slot did not take. A THIRD exception goes in ../writableLine4cThirdElection, which refuses the return whenever it is answered, because every triple puts a rollover beside an exclusion. FEEDS: ../line4cSecondElection, and through it ../hasQcdElection and ../hasHfdElection, which ../qcdElectedAmount, ../isSupportedQcdElection, ../hfdElectedAmount and ../isSupportedHfdElection read; ../line4cQcdExclusion and ../line4cHfdExclusion follow those without a body change, so both subtrahends of ../line4bTaxableAmount can be positive on one form. The per-exception AMOUNTS are the slots that already ship, ../writableQcdAmount and ../writableHfdAmount; this slot adds no amount of its own. THE STATEMENT ITSELF is an attachment, and what this dictionary lacks is a FREE-TEXT attachment idiom rather than an attachment idiom as such: the BOOLEAN one exists and works, /writableForm5329Line54ReasonableCauseStatementAttached recording that the filer collected the statement and /form5329Line54WaiverRequiresReasonableCauseStatement carrying the obligation to the render layer, with Schedule F and Form 4835 on the same shape. Here the statement's CONTENT is already derivable from ../writableQcdAmount and ../writableHfdAmount, so that pair is the precedent a successor should follow; it is a named gap rather than something improvised inside this module.

Fact.Name: The SECOND line 4c election in force for this Form 1099-R
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of ../writableLine4cSecondElection, the exact shape of ../line4cElection beside it: resolves the "none" option when the writable is unanswered and on any form that is not IRA-flagged, because line 4c belongs to line 4. Never Incomplete, so every consumer reads it without an IsComplete wrapper of its own.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4c - a THIRD box checked for this Form 1099-R
Fact.Description:
ASK: "Does a third line 4c exception also apply to this IRA distribution?" and, if so, which one. HELP: line 4c prints three boxes, and the printed instruction says that if more than one exception applies you check a box for each and attach a statement showing the amount of each ("Line 4b - $1,000 Rollover and $500 HFD"); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 28. ASKED WHEN: the form's IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked AND ../writableLine4cSecondElection is already answered with something other than "none" - a lone exception belongs in the first slot and a pair in the first two. UNANSWERED: no third exception; the form behaves exactly as it did before this slot existed, and nothing is Incomplete.
VALIDATION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SLOT: THERE IS NO SUPPORTED TRIPLE. The only pair this dictionary computes is a QCD in one slot and an HFD in another, so every three-box combination contains a rollover, and a rollover beside either exclusion already fails ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection. Any answer here other than "none" therefore refuses the return through ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution and /knockoutIraSepSimple, and the application should say so on the screen rather than let the filer meet it at submission.
WHAT THE SLOT BUYS IS A VISIBLE REFUSAL IN PLACE OF A SILENT OVER-STATEMENT. Before it, a filer to whom three exceptions applied could enter only two; entering the two that compute filed a return that dropped the third exception without a word and over-stated line 4b by the dropped amount. Three slots is also the maximum the printed row can carry - line 4c prints exactly three boxes ("c Check if (see instructions) . . . 1 Rollover 2 QCD 3"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040.pdf, page 1) - so the vocabulary now saturates the form and a fourth slot is not expressible on it.
FEEDS: ../line4cThirdElection, and through it ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection's FIRST Case; also ../hasQcdElection and ../hasHfdElection, which span every slot. The per-exception AMOUNTS are the slots that already ship, ../writableQcdAmount and ../writableHfdAmount; this slot adds no amount of its own.

Fact.Name: The THIRD line 4c election in force for this Form 1099-R
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of ../writableLine4cThirdElection, the exact shape of ../line4cElection and ../line4cSecondElection beside it: resolves the "none" option when the writable is unanswered and on any form that is not IRA-flagged, because line 4c belongs to line 4. Never Incomplete, so every consumer reads it without an IsComplete wrapper of its own.

Fact.Name: Line 4c box 2 is checked for this Form 1099-R, in any slot
Fact.Description: TRUE when the qualified-charitable-distribution box is the election in ANY of the three line 4c slots - ../line4cElection, ../line4cSecondElection or ../line4cThirdElection. It is the ONE reading of "box 2 is checked" in this module: ../qcdElectedAmount, ../isSupportedQcdElection and ../qcdElectedOnCodeOneContradictsAge all read it rather than comparing an election themselves, and /anyLine4cQcdElection aggregates it to the printed box, so a QCD entered as the second or third exception is treated exactly like one entered as the first. A QCD in the THIRD slot never reaches a filable return - ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection's first Case refuses any answered third slot - but this fact still spans it, because a predicate that claims to be the one reading of a box must read every slot the module offers. All three inputs are complete-safe, so this is Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: Line 4c box 3 is checked for this Form 1099-R, in any slot
Fact.Description: TRUE when the HSA-funding-distribution box is the election in ANY of the three line 4c slots - ../line4cElection, ../line4cSecondElection or ../line4cThirdElection. The box-3 twin of ../hasQcdElection and the one reading of "box 3 is checked" in this module: ../hfdElectedAmount and ../isSupportedHfdElection read it rather than comparing an election themselves, and /anyLine4cHfdElection aggregates it to the printed box. An HFD in the third slot never reaches a filable return, for the reason ../hasQcdElection gives, and this fact spans it on the same footing. All three inputs are complete-safe, so this is Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: Box 1 checked on a fully rolled-over direct rollover: the one line 4c shape that computes
Fact.Description:
The single line-4c election whose printed treatment this dictionary can produce with facts it already has. Three conditions, and each is doing work.
(a) BOX 1 IS CHECKED (../line4cElection is "rollover"). Exception 1 is the filer's assertion that the distribution was rolled over, and no Form 1099-R can carry it: the custodian reports the movement, not the filer's intent. Without this the shape is indistinguishable from an ordinary distribution the filer kept.
(b) IT IS A DIRECT ROLLOVER (../isDirectRollover, box 7 G or H). This is the half of Exception 1 the FORM corroborates. The INDIRECT half is deliberately left out: a 60-day rollover on a code 1/2/3/7 form is already refused by /flowKnockoutForRollover through ../causesRolloverKO, a return-level knockout that is NOT gated on ../notIraSepSimple and therefore already sees IRA-flagged forms. Admitting the indirect half here would mean reaching into that knockout's population, which belongs to the pension side of this module and is a different unit. So an indirect rollover election stays refused, by ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection when the filer did not indicate the indirect rollover and by /flowKnockoutForRollover when they did.
(c) BOX 2a IS $0, which is what makes this the FULL rollover rather than a partial one. Exception 1 branches on exactly that: "If the total distribution was rolled over, enter -0- on line 4b. If the total distribution wasn't rolled over, enter the part not rolled over on line 4b unless Exception 2 applies to the part not rolled over." Only the first branch is computable from what ships - the second needs an intake for the not-rolled-over part. A direct rollover reported with a taxable part (box 2a above $0) therefore stays refused, by clause (1) of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution, which the Switch reaches immediately after this one.
WHY NO ARITHMETIC IS OWED FOR THIS ARM, which is the reason the income module needed no body change. Line 4b for this item is $0, and box 2a IS $0 by condition (c), so income:/taxableIraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs - already a CollectionSum of box 2a - sums it correctly with no term added. Line 4a is the gross, and income:/iraDistributions already selects the collection total whenever gross differs from taxable, a disjunct that was authored as unreachable-but-kept and that this unit MAKES reachable. Both printed instructions are produced by bodies that already ship.
NAMED, NOT FIXED: Exception 1 adds that a rollover into a QUALIFIED PLAN, or one made in 2026, needs "a statement explaining what you did" attached to the return. An IRA-flagged code-G form cannot be told apart from an IRA-to-IRA rollover here, so a return this arm admits may be one that owes that statement. Attachments are the application / MeF surface rather than this repo (invariant 7), so it is recorded here rather than refused.
COMPLETE-SAFE on an unanswered box 7: ../distributionCode is Incomplete when the code is blank, so the first Case returns false rather than letting an Incomplete leak into the All. Such a form is refused for its missing code by /knockoutForForm1099RDistributionCode in any event.

Fact.Name: Box 1 checked on a PARTLY rolled-over direct rollover: Exception 1's second branch
Fact.Description:
The other half of Exception 1, and the sibling of ../isFullDirectRolloverElection. The printed rule is two consecutive sentences and they split on one fact: "If the total distribution was rolled over, enter -0- on line 4b. If the total distribution wasn't rolled over, enter the part not rolled over on line 4b unless Exception 2 applies to the part not rolled over." The first sentence is the sibling; this fact is the second.
FOUR CONDITIONS. The first two are the sibling's, unchanged and unrestated; the two inequalities are what make this the PARTIAL branch.
(a) BOX 1 IS CHECKED (../line4cElection is "rollover") and (b) IT IS A DIRECT ROLLOVER (../isDirectRollover, box 7 G or H). Identical to the sibling and for identical reasons: no Form 1099-R can carry the filer's rollover intent, and the INDIRECT half stays where the sibling left it, with /flowKnockoutForRollover on an indicated indirect rollover and with ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection otherwise. This unit does not reach into that population.
(c) BOX 2a IS ABOVE $0. This is what separates the two arms and it separates them COMPLETELY: the sibling requires box 2a to EQUAL $0 and this one requires it to EXCEED $0, so no form can satisfy both and their order in any Switch is free.
(d) BOX 2a IS BELOW BOX 1. Exception 1 opens "if you rolled over part or all of the distribution", so a form whose taxable amount is the whole gross had NOTHING rolled over and is not inside the Exception at all. It stays refused by clause (2) of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution, the un-elected direct rollover clause, which is the pre-existing answer for a code G or H form the filer has no honourable election for. The condition also bounds the arithmetic: line 4b can never exceed line 4a on a form this arm admits.
WHY NO INTAKE IS OWED FOR "THE PART NOT ROLLED OVER": the printed sentence writes the NOT rolled over part straight onto line 4b. Inside Exception 1's scope the rolled-over part is NEVER taxable. The Exception lists exactly two movements: a Roth IRA to another Roth IRA, and an IRA other than a Roth IRA to a qualified plan or another IRA other than a Roth IRA. A conversion INTO a Roth IRA, the one rollover shape that is taxable in full, is excluded by that list's own parentheses. And the BASIS population is held away by income:/knockoutIraDistributionDoubleIntake, which blocks submission when an IRA-flagged Form 1099-R co-exists with a claimed Form 8606, so Exception 1's "unless Exception 2 applies to the part not rolled over" cannot bite on any form that reaches here. With no basis and an untaxed rolled part, the taxable amount the custodian reports in box 2a and the part not rolled over are the same dollars. That is DERIVED from the printed scope, not assumed from the module's box-2a-as-reported convention, and it is why this unit ships no writable: an intake would have had to equal box 2a to be honoured, and would have moved no dollar on any return.
SO THE ARITHMETIC ALREADY SHIPS, exactly as it did for the sibling. Line 4b for this item is box 2a, and income:/taxableIraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs is already a CollectionSum of box 2a. Line 4a is the gross, and income:/iraDistributions selects the collection total whenever gross differs from taxable, which condition (d) guarantees. No income-module body change is owed; only the prose there that named the sibling as the ONLY admitted shape in which the two totals differ.
COMPLETE-SAFE on an unanswered box 7, by the sibling's leading Case verbatim: ../distributionCode is Incomplete when the code is blank, so the All is never evaluated with an Incomplete inside it, and such a form is refused by /knockoutForForm1099RDistributionCode in any event.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4b - the part of this distribution that was a QCD
Fact.Description:
User response: how much of this IRA distribution the trustee paid directly to a qualifying charity. A Form 1099-R cannot carry it - see the block comment above - and Exception 3 branches on it: the whole distribution being a QCD gives -0- on line 4b, and part of it being a QCD puts "the part that is not a QCD" there.
PER ITEM, matching ../writableLine4cElection, because the Exception applies distribution by distribution. NOT ASKED unless that election is "qcd": ../qcdElectedAmount reads it through an election test, so an amount answered under any other election moves no dollar.
NOT BOUNDED BY A DECLARED Limit against box 1, although it looks like it should be. A Max Limit takes a literal here, and the bound this input needs is the item's own box 2a - so the comparison lives in ../isSupportedQcdElection instead, where exceeding it is a visible refusal rather than a silent clamp. The Min $0 Limit IS declared, matching ../writableTaxableAmount.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4c - the one-time QCD to a split-interest entity
Fact.Description:
User response: whether this distribution is the taxpayer's ONE-TIME election to treat a distribution to a split-interest entity (a charitable remainder annuity trust, a charitable remainder unitrust or a charitable gift annuity) as a QCD.
WHY THIS INTAKE EXISTS AT ALL, when the SIE election has its own printed reporting. Pub 590-B says the one-time SIE election is reported by checking box 3 on line 4c and writing "SIE" in the entry space, which would arrive here as the "hfd" option and be refused with the rest of box 3. That routing is not something this dictionary can rely on: the intake ../writableLine4cElection offers a filer four labels (none / rollover / qcd / hfd) and an SIE distribution IS a qualified charitable distribution, so a filer choosing among those labels picks "qcd". Without this question the $54,000 SIE sub-ceiling would go unenforced underneath the $108,000 one, and the error direction is UNDERSTATEMENT of income.
ANSWERED TRUE IS A REFUSAL, not a smaller ceiling, and the ground is not only the sub-ceiling: the SIE election requires a statement attached to the return (the attachment must say the election was not made in a prior year, and describe the income interest), and an attachment is the MeF / the application surface rather than this repo (invariant 7). It is also a LIFETIME election, which one tax year's data cannot verify. So no $54,000 literal is written and none is owed.
ANSWERED FALSE IS REQUIRED, not assumed. ../isSupportedQcdElection tests IsComplete on this fact, so an unanswered box leaves the election refused. Defaulting it to false would let a filer who was never asked the question be over-excluded, which is the direction this fact exists to close.

Fact.Name: The recipient was old enough for a QCD on every day of the tax year
Fact.Description:
Whether this form's recipient can be placed at or above the QCD age threshold for the WHOLE of 2025, from a date of birth alone.
THE PRINTED CONDITION is "You must have been at least age 70 1/2 when the distribution was made" (IRC 408(d)(8)(B)(ii) puts it as "made on or after the date that the individual ... has attained age 70 1/2"). It is a condition on the DISTRIBUTION DATE, and no fact in this dictionary carries the date of a Form 1099-R distribution.
SO THIS IS A SUFFICIENT BOUND, NOT THE CONDITION. A recipient born on or before 1954-06-30 had passed their 70th birthday by 2024-06-30 and so was more than half a year past it on 2025-01-01, the earliest day a 2025 distribution could have been made - therefore at least age 70 1/2 on every such day, whatever the date was. The bound decides the cohort it can decide and refuses the rest; it never admits a form the printed condition would exclude.
WHY 1954-06-30 AND NOT SOMETHING LATER, and why the bound still needs no convention. The six-calendar-month convention - that a person attains age 70 1/2 exactly six calendar months after their 70th birthday - is NOT PRINTED in any source vendored in this repo: it appears in neither the Form 1040 instructions, nor Pub 590-A, nor Pub 590-B, nor IRC 408, each of which uses the phrase "age 70 1/2" without defining it. Searched, not assumed. So the bound is chosen to be right under EVERY reading of "half a year" rather than under one of them. A recipient born 1954-06-30 turned 70 on 2024-06-30; by 2025-01-01, the earliest day a 2025 distribution could have been made, 185 days had passed, which exceeds half of any year (182.5 days of 365) and also exceeds six calendar months. Both readings agree, so no convention is being relied on.
THE COST IS STILL NAMED, and it is now six months smaller. A recipient born on or after 1954-07-01 is refused here, though under the six-calendar-month reading a 1954-07-01 birth is exactly 70 1/2 on 2025-01-01, and any later birth may still satisfy the printed condition at the ACTUAL distribution date, which no fact in this dictionary carries. That residue ends when the distribution date, or the age condition on it, becomes intake, or when a source that defines "age 70 1/2" becomes obtainable.
COMPLETE-SAFE on a missing date of birth: the first Case returns false rather than letting an Incomplete escape into the conjunction that reads this.

Fact.Name: The QCD amount claimed on this form
Fact.Description:
The amount ../writableQcdAmount carries when this form actually claims a QCD, and $0 otherwise. Two guards, and the first one is structural rather than about the tax law: ../hasQcdElection - "box 2 is checked in EITHER line 4c slot" - is never Incomplete, because both ../line4cElection and ../line4cSecondElection are complete-safe, so testing it FIRST makes this fact Complete on every form in every return - which matters because the per-filer totals below sum it across a whole collection and any Incomplete item would collapse the sum, and that sum is read by a knockout.
THIS IS THE CEILING'S MEASURE, not the excluded amount: ../line4cQcdExclusion is what reaches line 4b, and it is $0 unless every condition in ../isSupportedQcdElection holds. The two are deliberately different facts because "how much did you say was a QCD" is the input to the ceiling test and "how much may be excluded" is its output.
AN ANSWERED $0 IS HONOURED HERE, WHICH DEPARTS FROM THIS DICTIONARY'S OTHER IRA INTAKE, so the departure is stated rather than left to be found. income:/hasPositiveIraDistributionScalarIntake makes an answered $0 behave like an unanswered one, because there a $0 answer would shadow a live Form 8606 route and silently drop a taxable amount. Nothing is shadowed here: a filer who checks box 2 and then states $0 of QCD gets an exclusion of $0, their whole box 2a on line 4b, and a FILABLE return - which is the correct printed outcome, since no part of the distribution was a QCD and Exception 3's line-4a rule does not apply to it. The only visible change from that answer is that the return files where an answered election used to be refused outright, and it files at the same numbers the pre-election dictionary produced. Refusing it instead would be an intake-contradiction refusal with no contradiction behind it.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's total QCDs for the year
Fact.Description:
The aggregate the annual ceiling applies to, for the primary filer. The ceiling is PER TAXPAYER - IRC 408(d)(8)(A) says "with respect to a taxpayer", and both the Form 1040 instructions and Pub 590-B spell out that a spouse on a joint return has their own - so the two filers get their own sums over the named per-filer collections this module already ships. No engine capability is needed for that and none was assumed: /primaryFiler1099Rs is an ordinary Filter, so this is a collection sum over a named collection.
GUARDED, not bare. /primaryFiler1099RTaxableAmounts sums the same collection with no guard and goes Incomplete when the filer has no Form 1099-R; its consumers absorb that. This sum cannot, because a knockout reads it, so it uses the IsComplete + CollectionSize pair /hasIraDistribution1099R uses and resolves Complete $0 on a return with no forms at all. NO Round: every term is already whole dollars (../qcdElectedAmount reads a Dollar writable that box 2a's own rounding bounds), and rounding a sum of whole dollars is a no-op.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's total QCDs for the year
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own aggregate for the annual ceiling, the sibling of /primaryFilerQcdTotal and guarded identically. A joint return's two filers each get the full ceiling, so the two sums are never added: /form1099Rs/*/isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling selects one of them per item by whose form it is.

Fact.Name: This form's filer is at or below the annual QCD ceiling
Fact.Description:
Whether the QCD total of the filer this form belongs to is at or below the printed annual ceiling. The comparison is INCLUSIVE - "can't be more than $108,000" - so a filer whose total is exactly the ceiling is inside it.
THIS FACT IS NO LONGER THE WHOLE GATE, and reading it as one would mis-describe the module. Pub 590-B prints the answer for a filer above the ceiling - "Any QCD in excess of the $108,000 exclusion limit is included in income as any other distribution" - and with a SINGLE QCD form that is an ordinary cap needing no allocation rule, which ../line4cQcdExclusion now applies. ../isSupportedQcdElection therefore accepts EITHER this fact or "this form is the filer's whole QCD total". What is still refused is the case the source does not answer: MORE THAN ONE QCD form for the same filer whose aggregate exceeds the ceiling, where nothing printed says which form's exclusion is cut and applying the whole excess to each would over-state income twice over. The refusal is visible (a knockout) and the allocation question is what a successor would have to answer.
WHICH FILER, decided by ../belongsToPrimaryFiler. A form whose recipient is neither filer cannot exist: ../filer is a CollectionItem into /filers with the primary as its Placeholder, and a secondary recipient without MFJ is already refused by /form1099Rs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ. So the else-arm is the secondary filer's ceiling rather than a third state.
WITNESSED IN ALL FOUR STATES, because the two arms are separate code and a shared ceiling would pass a primary-only test.

Fact.Name: This form's filer made no traditional IRA contribution that would offset a QCD
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer this form belongs to is clear of the QCD offset rule.
THE RULE, which is easy to miss because the Form 1040 instructions do not print it. IRC 408(d)(8)(A) reduces the excludable QCD by the excess of the taxpayer's aggregate section 219 deductions for all years ending on or after they attained age 70 1/2 over the amounts already used to reduce QCDs in earlier years - the "Offset of QCDs by amounts contributed after age 70 1/2" paragraph in Pub 590-B, computed on its Appendix D worksheet. A filer who deducts a traditional IRA contribution while taking a QCD does not get both in full.
WHAT THIS FACT TESTS, AND WHY IT IS WIDER THAN THE RULE. The rule is about the DEDUCTION allowed under section 219. This fact tests the CONTRIBUTION intake instead, and refuses whenever it is positive. Two reasons, and the first is not a preference. (1) ACYCLICITY: iraDeduction:/primaryFilerTraditionalIraDeduction is downstream of MAGI, which is downstream of total income, which is downstream of Form 1040 line 4b - which is what this chain computes. Reading the deduction here would close a cycle in a graph whose engine has no cycle detection (the same trap iraDeduction and form8606 document at length around the section 219(g) bound). The contribution is a plain Writable and closes nothing. (2) A contribution is at least as large as the deduction it can produce, so refusing on a positive contribution refuses a SUPERSET of the returns the rule reaches: over-refusal, never under-statement.
THE PRIOR-YEAR HALF IS NOW COVERED TOO, BY A SIBLING RATHER THAN BY THIS FACT. The offset also counts deductions from PRIOR years in which the filer was already 70 1/2, and no return carried that history. The contract filled - /primaryFilerQcdOffsetCarryover collects the history and /form1099Rs/*/qcdPostSeventyContributionOffset computes Pub 590-B's Appendix D reduction from it - so the two facts now partition the rule. THIS fact stays as it is and stays WIDER than its half: it refuses a positive current-year contribution outright rather than feeding it into the worksheet's line 2, so the worksheet's line 2 is $0 on every form that reaches an exclusion and the sibling's arithmetic has one term to add.
COMPLETE-SAFE: an unanswered contribution intake is read as no contribution, the IsComplete-guarded shape income:/hasPositiveIraDistributionScalarIntake uses for the same question about a different intake.

Fact.Name: QCD Adjustment Worksheet line 1 - the primary filer's prior-year IRA deductions taken at age 70 1/2 or older
Fact.Description:
User response: the total traditional IRA contributions the PRIMARY filer deducted in EARLIER years while age 70 1/2 or older that have not already reduced the excludable amount of a qualified charitable distribution in an earlier year. No Form 1099-R carries it and no current-year figure implies it, so it is a genuine taxpayer input, modelled ahead of its screen under the BUILD-FIRST directive.
IT IS ONE NUMBER WHERE THE STATUTE HAS TWO, and a screen author needs to know why. IRC 408(d)(8)(A) subtracts clause (ii), the reductions already taken in earlier years, from clause (i), the aggregate section 219 deductions allowed for every taxable year ending on or after the filer attained age 70 1/2. Pub 590-B's Appendix D worksheet nets the two into its line 1 and carries the net from one year's worksheet to the next. That net is what this intake collects, so nothing here has to reconstruct a year-by-year history.
IT IS ALSO WORKSHEET LINE 2's FIRST-WORKSHEET CLAUSE, and that is not a merge of convenience. Line 2 collects the CURRENT year's deducted contribution and adds "If this is your first QCD worksheet, also include contributions you deducted in prior years during which you were age 70 1/2 (or older) at the end of the year". Those prior-year deductions are the same quantity line 1 carries for a returning filer; the worksheet splits them only because a first-time filer has no prior worksheet to carry from. A filer answering this question states the prior-year total whether or not they have ever filled one in.
THE CURRENT-YEAR HALF OF LINE 2 IS NOT ASKED HERE, because /form1099Rs/*/hasNoQcdOffsettingIraContribution already refuses every QCD election on a return whose current-year traditional IRA CONTRIBUTION intake is positive. On every form that reaches an exclusion, line 2's own term is therefore $0, and the two facts partition the printed rule rather than overlapping it. Pub 590-B's published Jim example straddles the partition: his 2025 worksheet is the current-year case the shipping guard refuses, and his 2026 worksheet is the prior-year case this intake answers.
AN ANSWER IS REQUIRED, NOT DEFAULTED, on /form1099Rs/*/writableIsQcdToSplitInterestEntity's precedent and for its reason: a filer who was never asked would otherwise be over-excluded, which is the error direction this intake exists to close. /form1099Rs/*/hasAnsweredQcdOffsetCarryover carries that requirement into /form1099Rs/*/isSupportedQcdElection, so an unanswered box leaves the election visibly refused instead of silently excluded in full.

Fact.Name: QCD Adjustment Worksheet line 1 - the secondary filer's prior-year IRA deductions taken at age 70 1/2 or older
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own worksheet line 1, the sibling of /primaryFilerQcdOffsetCarryover and argued there. It is a SEPARATE intake because the offset, like the annual ceiling above it, is a per-TAXPAYER figure: IRC 408(d)(8)(A) reduces "the amount of distributions not includible in gross income ... with respect to a taxpayer", and a spouse on a joint return runs their own worksheet. The two are never added - /form1099Rs/*/qcdOffsetCarryover picks one of them per item by whose form it is, exactly as /form1099Rs/*/isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling picks between the two QCD totals.

Fact.Name: QCD Adjustment Worksheet line 3 for the filer this form belongs to
Fact.Description:
The worksheet's line 3 - line 1 plus line 2 - for the filer whose form this is.
IT EQUALS LINE 1 ON EVERY FORM THAT REACHES AN EXCLUSION, because line 2's current-year term is $0 there by construction: ../hasNoQcdOffsettingIraContribution refuses any QCD election on a return whose current-year traditional IRA contribution intake is positive, and line 2's first-worksheet clause is already inside the line-1 intake by that intake's own definition. So the addition the worksheet prints has one non-zero term and is not written as an Add.
WHICH FILER, decided by ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, on /form1099Rs/*/isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling's precedent: a form whose recipient is neither filer cannot exist, so the else-arm is the secondary filer's figure rather than a third state.
COMPLETE-SAFE at $0 on an unanswered intake, so this fact never goes Incomplete and can never collapse ../line4bTaxableAmount. The $0 is defensive only, and is NOT how an unanswered box is treated: ../hasAnsweredQcdOffsetCarryover refuses the election outright in that case, so the exclusion is $0 rather than computed against a guessed carryover.

Fact.Name: This form's filer has stated their post-70 1/2 IRA deduction history
Fact.Description:
Whether the worksheet line-1 intake is answered for the filer this form belongs to.
A SEPARATE FACT FROM ../qcdOffsetCarryover BECAUSE THE TWO ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. That fact reads an unanswered intake as $0 so it can never go Incomplete; this one reports the unanswered state so ../isSupportedQcdElection can refuse it. Without the split, a filer who was never asked would be excluded in full - the silent under-statement this whole sub-chain exists to close - and the Description of ../writableIsQcdToSplitInterestEntity makes the identical argument for the identical shape.
ALWAYS COMPLETE: an IsComplete inside a Switch on ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, which is itself never Incomplete, so putting this inside ../isSupportedQcdElection's completeness Case cannot make that fact Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This form can carry the whole of its filer's QCD offset
Fact.Description:
Whether the worksheet's per-TAXPAYER reduction can be attributed to this one form without inventing an allocation rule.
THE PROBLEM, AND IT IS THE CEILING'S PROBLEM AGAIN. The worksheet computes ONE excludable amount for the filer (line 4 less line 3), while Form 1040 line 4b is a sum of per-distribution taxable amounts, so this dictionary carries the exclusion per item. With one QCD form the reduction lands on that form and the arithmetic is the worksheet's. With two, nothing printed says which form's exclusion is cut, and applying the whole reduction to each would over-state income by counting it twice.
SO THE MULTI-FORM CASE IS REFUSED RATHER THAN ALLOCATED, on the precedent ../isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling sets for the identical shape: rather than invent an allocation rule for the multi-form case and compute the single-form case, refuse both and say so. The refusal is visible (a knockout), and the allocation question is what a successor would answer. It is NOT a new gap in the roadmap sense - it is the same unanswered allocation question the ceiling already records, reached from a second direction.
THREE WAYS TO BE ALLOCABLE, and the first two keep the refusal off returns it has no business touching. (1) THE FILER HAS NO OFFSET at all, which is every filer whose worksheet line 1 is $0 - so the multi-form QCD returns this dictionary already computes keep computing, and the refusal costs nothing where the rule does not bite. (2) THIS FORM CLAIMS NO QCD, in which case its reduction is $0 whatever the filer's history is. (3) THIS FORM'S QCD IS THE FILER'S WHOLE QCD TOTAL, which is the single-form case stated without counting forms: if the totals agree, no sibling form is carrying any of the same reduction.

Fact.Name: The QCD reduction for traditional IRA contributions deducted after age 70 1/2
Fact.Description:
The amount by which this form's QCD exclusion is reduced because the filer deducted traditional IRA contributions in years they were already age 70 1/2 or older. Pub 590-B's Appendix D worksheet computes it: line 5 subtracts line 3 from line 4, and this fact is the line-3 term as it is actually taken off, never more than the QCD it reduces.
THE MIN IS THE STATUTE'S CLAMP, moved. IRC 408(d)(8)(A) reduces the excludable amount "(but not below zero)", and the worksheet says the same thing in its footnote ("If zero or less, you have no excludable qualified charitable distribution"). Bounding the REDUCTION by the elected amount is that clamp expressed where the subtraction can see it, so ../line4cQcdExclusion never has to test for a negative result. It also gives the Max - the elected QCD amount - structurally, which a declared Limit could not: a Limit takes a literal, and a Dependency inside a Writable is exactly the shape that closes cycles the JS dependency check is blind to.
$0 ON EVERY FORM THAT IS NOT A QCD, with no arm of its own: ../qcdElectedAmount is already $0 unless the election is "qcd" and answered, so the min of anything and $0 is $0. That is why this fact carries no election test and cannot make a non-QCD form Incomplete.
THE CARRY-FORWARD FOOTNOTE IS NOT MODELLED, and it is not owed. The worksheet tells a filer whose line 5 is negative to enter the shortfall as a positive amount on line 1 of NEXT year's worksheet. That is a TY2026 input, collected by TY2026's own copy of /primaryFilerQcdOffsetCarryover; nothing on this year's Form 1040 reports it.
WHAT THIS FILLS. The fill supersedes the alternative rather than choosing between them: requiring the intake to be ANSWERED makes the silence visible exactly as an attestation would, and answering it with an amount computes the reduced exclusion where an attestation could only refuse. The contract's "two running carryovers" is one intake here, for the reason /primaryFilerQcdOffsetCarryover records.

Fact.Name: Box 2 checked on a QCD this dictionary can compute
Fact.Description:
The QCD elections whose printed treatment this dictionary produces. Every conjunct is doing work and each has its own refusal witness among the node tests, so a mis-wired one cannot hide behind a sibling.
(a) BOX 2 IS CHECKED (../hasQcdElection, which is "qcd" in EITHER line 4c slot - ../line4cElection or ../line4cSecondElection), tested FIRST and in its own Case so the conjunction below is never evaluated - and never made Incomplete - on the forms that are not QCD elections. This conjunct is also half of the two-box pair test: ../hasUnsupportedLine4c Election refuses a form with a second box unless THIS fact and ../isSupportedHfdElection are both true, so a QCD in the second slot reaches line 4b only alongside a supported HFD.
(b) THE QCD AMOUNT IS ANSWERED. Without it there is nothing to take off line 4b, and the election stays refused. This is the intake the block comment above argues for.
(c) THE AMOUNT IS NOT MORE THAN BOX 2a. A QCD is a QCD "only to the extent that the distribution would be includible in gross income" (IRC 408(d)(8)(B)). On the forms this arm admits box 2a is the whole distribution, so an amount above it is a contradictory answer rather than a capping situation, and it is refused rather than silently clamped.
(d) BOX 2a EQUALS BOX 1 AND IS ABOVE $0. This is the QCD's signature on the form: the custodian reports the distribution as fully taxable because it does not know where the money went. A form whose box 2a is BELOW box 1 has basis or another Exception in play, which is Exception 2's Form 8606 territory and is already refused by clause 1 of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution; the condition is repeated here so this fact is true only where its own arithmetic is right, not because the refusal was in doubt. Box 2a above $0 keeps the arm off a form with nothing to exclude, which clause 0 of that same fact refuses for a different reason.
(e) THE RECIPIENT IS OLD ENOUGH ALL YEAR (../isQcdEligibleByAge), (f) THE ANNUAL CEILING IS SATISFIED OR IS AN ORDINARY CAP - either the filer's aggregate is at or below it (../isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling) OR this form IS the filer's whole QCD total, in which case ../line4cQcdExclusion caps at $108,000 and the excess falls through to line 4b with nothing to allocate; only a filer with MORE THAN ONE QCD form over the ceiling is refused, because nothing printed says which form's exclusion is cut, (g) THE FILER HAS NO OFFSETTING IRA CONTRIBUTION THIS YEAR (../hasNoQcdOffsettingIraContribution) and (h) THIS IS NOT THE ONE-TIME SPLIT-INTEREST-ENTITY ELECTION, which must be answered false rather than left blank. Each is argued on its own fact.
(i) THE FILER'S POST-70 1/2 DEDUCTION HISTORY IS ANSWERED (../hasAnsweredQcdOffsetCarryover), which rides in the completeness Case above with (b) and (h) rather than in this All, and (j) THE OFFSET THAT HISTORY PRODUCES LANDS ON A SINGLE FORM (../isQcdOffsetAllocable). The pair is the prior-year half of the same section 219 offset (g) covers for the current year: (g) reads an intake this return already carries and refuses when it is positive, while (i) and (j) gate an intake this dictionary had to add, because no return carries a filer's earlier years.
NAMED, NOT FIXED - the printed caution this dictionary cannot enforce. "You can't claim a charitable contribution deduction for any QCD not included in your income" (Pub 590-B; IRC 408(d)(8)(E) as "Denial of deduction"). A filer who excludes a QCD here and also enters the same gift among their Schedule A charitable contributions takes the benefit twice, and nothing in the data distinguishes that from two genuinely separate gifts - the Schedule A intake is a total, not a list of donees. It is recorded here rather than refused, on the precedent of Exception 1's qualified-plan statement on ../isFullDirectRolloverElection.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4b - the QCD amount excluded from this IRA distribution
Fact.Description:
The part of this distribution that line 4b leaves out because it was a qualified charitable distribution. $0 unless ../isSupportedQcdElection holds, and when it does, the elected amount CAPPED AT THE ANNUAL CEILING less its post-70 1/2 offset, floored at $0.
THE SUBTRACTION IS PUB 590-B's WORKSHEET LINE 5, "Subtract line 3 from line 4. This is the amount of your excludable qualified charitable distribution for the current year", and it was added after this fact first shipped: the exclusion used to pass ../qcdElectedAmount straight through, which is right only for a filer with no post-70 1/2 IRA deduction history. NEVER NEGATIVE: the statute's own parenthetical, "shall be reduced (but not below zero)" in IRC 408(d)(8)(A), is carried by an explicit GreaterOf($0) floor. It USED to be carried by the fact that ../qcdPostSeventyContributionOffset is bounded by the elected amount, which stopped being sufficient the moment the minuend became the CAPPED amount rather than the elected one.
THE CEILING IS A CAP, NOT A GATE, and that is the second change. IRC 408(d)(8)(A) excludes "So much of the aggregate amount ... as does not exceed" the ceiling, and Pub 590-B prints the disposition of the rest outright: "Any QCD in excess of the $108,000 exclusion limit is included in income as any other distribution". So the minuend is LesserOf(elected, $108,000) and the excess falls through to Form 1040 line 4b through ../line4bTaxableAmount. The ORDER is the statute's: cap first, then reduce by the post-70 1/2 offset, then floor. What stays refused is the case the source does not answer - a filer with MORE THAN ONE QCD form whose aggregate exceeds the ceiling, where nothing printed says which form's exclusion is cut.
THE PRINTED RULE IS TWO SENTENCES AND THIS FACT IS BOTH OF THEM, up to the ceiling. "If the total amount distributed is a QCD, enter -0- on line 4b" is this exclusion equalling box 2a; "If only part of the distribution is a QCD, enter the part that is not a QCD on line 4b" is it being less. ../line4bTaxableAmount does the subtraction, so neither sentence is special-cased - and above the ceiling the first sentence yields to Pub 590-B's own "Any QCD in excess of the $108,000 exclusion limit is included in income as any other distribution", which the cap produces without a third rule.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT TOUCH IS LINE 4a, and that is not an omission. Exception 3 opens "enter the total distribution on line 4a", and income:/iraDistributions already carries the collection gross whenever the gross total differs from the line-4b total - a disjunct authored for Exception 1 that this Exception reaches for the same structural reason. So line 4a needs no term and gets none.
THE HFD HALF OF THIS EXCLUSION IS A SEPARATE FACT, ../line4cHfdExclusion; nothing here computes it.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4b - the part of this distribution that was an HSA funding distribution
Fact.Description:
User response: how much of this IRA distribution the trustee transferred directly into the filer's HSA and the filer elects to keep out of income. The Form 1099-R cannot carry it - see the block comment above - and Exception 4 branches on it exactly as Exception 3 branches on the QCD amount: the whole distribution being an HFD gives -0- on line 4b, and part of it being an HFD puts "the part that isn't an HFD" there.
PER ITEM, matching ../writableLine4cElection, because the Exception applies distribution by distribution. NOT ASKED unless that election is "hfd": ../hfdElectedAmount reads it through an election test, so an amount answered under any other election moves no dollar.
NOT BOUNDED BY A DECLARED Limit against box 1 or against the HSA contribution limit, for ../writableQcdAmount's reason: a Max Limit takes a literal, and both bounds this input needs are computed. They live in ../isSupportedHfdElection, where exceeding either is a visible refusal rather than a silent clamp. The Min $0 Limit IS declared, matching its QCD sibling.

Fact.Name: The HFD amount claimed on this form
Fact.Description:
The amount ../writableHfdAmount carries when this form actually claims an HFD, and $0 otherwise. The election test comes FIRST and in its own Case, on ../qcdElectedAmount's precedent: ../hasHfdElection - "box 3 is checked in EITHER line 4c slot" - is never Incomplete, because both ../line4cElection and ../line4cSecondElection are complete-safe, so testing it first makes this fact Complete on every form without evaluating an unanswered intake.
THIS IS THE CAP'S MEASURE, not the excluded amount. ../line4cHfdExclusion is what reaches line 4b and it is $0 unless every condition in ../isSupportedHfdElection holds; this fact is what the filer SAID was an HFD, which is the figure the HSA contribution limit is tested against and the figure Form 8889 line 10 reports. The two are deliberately different facts for the reason its QCD sibling gives.
A FILER WHO CHECKS BOX 3 AND THEN STATES $0 gets an exclusion of $0 and a line 4b equal to box 2a, which is the right answer rather than a shadowed one: no part of the distribution was an HFD.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4c box 3 - this entry is the one-time SIE QCD, not an HFD
Fact.Description:
User response: whether the filer checked box 3 for Pub 590-B's one-time qualified charitable distribution to a split-interest entity rather than for an HSA funding distribution.
WHY THIS INTAKE EXISTS, and it is the mirror image of ../writableIsQcdToSplitInterestEntity. Box 3 carries TWO elections under one printed checkbox. The Form 1040 instructions tell an HFD filer to check box 3 and write "HFD" in the entry space; Pub 590-B tells an SIE filer to check the SAME box 3 and write "SIE" there. ../writableLine4cElection offers four labels and spells box 3 as "hfd", so a filer following Pub 590-B's box number lands on this option with an SIE election in hand. The QCD half closed the exposure that arrives under the "qcd" label; this closes the one that arrives under "hfd", and the two questions together make the box symmetric.
ANSWERED TRUE IS A REFUSAL, on exactly the grounds its sibling records: the SIE election requires a statement attached to the return, which is the MeF / the application surface rather than this repo (invariant 7), and it is a LIFETIME election one tax year's data cannot verify. No $54,000 literal is written and none is owed, because the election is refused rather than capped.
ANSWERED FALSE IS REQUIRED, not assumed. ../isSupportedHfdElection tests IsComplete on this fact, so an unanswered box leaves the election refused. Defaulting it to false would let a filer who was never asked be treated as making the election the dictionary can compute, when they may be making the one it cannot.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 10 - the primary filer's HSA funding distributions for the year
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's total elected HFD, summed over the named per-filer collection this module already ships. It is the figure the HSA contribution limit is tested against and the figure hsa:/filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionsTotal reports on Form 8889 line 10.
WHY THE ELECTED AMOUNT RATHER THAN THE EXCLUDED ONE, which are different facts. Form 8889 line 10 reports the QUALIFIED HSA funding distribution, and a distribution is qualified because the filer elected it out of income - so on any return that can be submitted the two figures are equal. They can differ only on a return where ../isSupportedHfdElection refuses the election, and that return is already refused by /knockoutIraSepSimple through /form1099Rs/*/hasUnsupportedLine4cElection, so no submittable return reports a line 10 the exclusion did not take. Summing the ELECTED amount is what keeps this fact out of a cycle: the exclusion reads the contribution limit, the contribution limit's Form 8889 line 6 reads line 11, and line 11 reads this fact.
GUARDED, not bare, on /primaryFilerQcdTotal's precedent and for its reason: a knockout reads this chain, so the IsComplete + CollectionSize pair keeps it Complete $0 on a return with no Form 1099-R at all. NO Round: ../hfdElectedAmount reads a Dollar writable and a sum of its values needs no second rounding, the same argument /primaryFilerQcdTotal makes.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 10 - the secondary filer's HSA funding distributions for the year
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own HFD total, the sibling of /primaryFilerHfdTotal and guarded identically. The exclusion is per INDIVIDUAL - IRC 408(d)(9) speaks of "the individual" throughout and Form 8889 is filed per spouse - so the two sums are never added: /form1099Rs/*/filerHfdTotal selects one of them per item by whose form it is, exactly as /form1099Rs/*/isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling selects between the two QCD totals.

Fact.Name: The HFD total of the filer this form belongs to
Fact.Description:
Whichever of /primaryFilerHfdTotal and /secondaryFilerHfdTotal belongs to this form's recipient, decided by ../belongsToPrimaryFiler on /form1099Rs/*/qcdOffsetCarryover's precedent: a form whose recipient is neither filer cannot exist, so the else-arm is the secondary filer's figure rather than a third state.
TWO USES, both in ../isSupportedHfdElection. It is the amount the HSA contribution limit is tested against, because that limit is per individual while the intake is per form. And it is how the single-distribution shape is stated without counting forms: an election whose amount equals the filer's whole total is the only HFD on the return for that filer.

Fact.Name: The primary filer has already used the once-in-a-lifetime HFD election
Fact.Description:
User response: whether this filer elected to exclude an HSA funding distribution from income in any earlier year.
WHY AN INTAKE AND NOT A DERIVATION. The election is once in a LIFETIME - IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(ii)(I) lets an individual make the election "only for one qualified HSA funding distribution during the lifetime of the individual", and the Form 1040 instructions and the Form 8889 instructions both repeat it - and nothing on this year's return can see an earlier year. The BUILD-FIRST directive licenses modelling the intake ahead of the screen that will collect it, and the shape is the QCD half's: an attestation whose SILENCE is a refusal.
PER FILER, not per form, because the rule is about the person. A joint return's two spouses each have their own lifetime, which is why this fact has a secondary sibling rather than being one return-level question.
AN ANSWER IS REQUIRED, NOT DEFAULTED, on /primaryFilerQcdOffsetCarryover's precedent: /form1099Rs/*/hasNoPriorLifetimeHfdElection reads this through an IsComplete, so an unanswered box leaves the election visibly refused rather than silently allowed. Answered TRUE is also a refusal - a second lifetime election is not a smaller exclusion, it is no exclusion.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer has already used the once-in-a-lifetime HFD election
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own lifetime attestation, the sibling of /primaryFilerHasPriorLifetimeHfdElection and argued there. It is a SEPARATE intake because the election belongs to an individual: a spouse who has never made one keeps their own election whatever the other spouse has done.

Fact.Name: This form's filer has stated they have never elected an HFD before
Fact.Description:
Whether the lifetime attestation is ANSWERED and answered NO for the filer this form belongs to. One fact rather than the QCD half's pair, because unlike a carryover amount there is nothing to read when the answer is missing: unanswered and answered-yes both mean the same thing here, which is that this dictionary will not compute the exclusion.
ALWAYS COMPLETE: an All of an IsComplete and a Boolean inside a Switch on ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, which is itself never Incomplete, so this fact can sit inside ../isSupportedHfdElection's conjunction without ever making it Incomplete. That is /form1099Rs/*/hasAnsweredQcdOffsetCarryover's argument for the identical shape.

Fact.Name: The HSA contribution limit the HFD exclusion is capped by
Fact.Description:
The printed ceiling on the exclusion, for the filer this form belongs to: Form 8889 line 3 plus line 7.
WHICH LIMIT, and it is derived from the printed sentence rather than picked. The Form 1040 instructions say "You can't exclude more than the limit on HSA contributions or more than the amount that would otherwise be included in your income", and the Form 8889 instructions sharpen the first half: "The maximum amount that can be excluded from income is based on your age at the end of the year and your HDHP coverage (self-only or family) at the time of the distribution." Age and coverage type are exactly what Form 8889 lines 3 and 7 carry - line 3 is the coverage-type annual limit including the section 223(b)(3) catch-up for an unmarried or self-only 55+ filer, and line 7 is that catch-up where a married family-coverage filer takes it instead. Their sum is the age-and-coverage limit the sentence names.
WHY NOT LINE 8, which is the module's own "total contribution limit" and looks like the obvious answer. Line 8 is line 6 plus line 7, and line 6 reaches hsa:/hsaPrimaryFilerContributionTotalLessAddition on the MFJ family-allocation path, which reads Form 8889 line 11 - and line 11 is line 9 plus line 10, where line 10 is the HFD total this unit computes. Capping on line 8 would close a dependency cycle through the very fact the cap feeds. Lines 3 and 7 are both clear of line 10: line 3 walks down through hsaBaseContributionLimit to the coverage constants, and line 7 reads only age, coverage and marital status. The MSA leg is inert as well - Form 8889 line 5 is line 3 unchanged while Archer MSAs are not modelled by this dictionary - so line 3 plus line 7 equals line 8 for every filer outside the allocation path.
INCOMPLETE OUTSIDE THE FORM 8889 POPULATION, deliberately. Both terms are Switches on hsa:/filers/*/hasMadeContributionsToHsa with no fallthrough, so this fact is Incomplete for a filer who is not completing Form 8889 Part I. That is the right shape and not a hazard: ../isSupportedHfdElection tests IsComplete on it in its own Case BEFORE the conjunction, so the Incompleteness is read as "this filer has no HSA contribution limit, so no HFD can be excluded" rather than leaking into line 4b. An HFD is a contribution to an HSA, so a filer with no HSA contributions cannot have made one.
THIS FACT IS NOT THE ONLY CEILING, and the paragraphs above are the record of the i1040gi half of the rule rather than the whole of it. They remain correct about what they identify - lines 3 plus 7 are the printed "limit on HSA contributions", and the cycle argument still holds - but the STATUTORY ceiling IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) states is the section 223(b) annual limitation computed on the coverage type in force AT THE TIME OF THE TRANSFER, which is line 3 with every month's coverage type replaced by the transfer month's. That figure ships at hsa:/filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap and reaches this module through ../hfdExclusionCap, which reads it where it is computable and THIS fact where it is not. The two are the same number for every filer whose coverage type did not change mid-year, which is why the substitution moves no committed case. This fact keeps every consumer it had: it is still conjunct (i)'s comparand and still the fallback ceiling.

Fact.Name: The 408(d)(9)(C)(i) cap is computable for the filer this form belongs to
Fact.Description:
Whether hsa:/filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable holds for this form's filer. That fact is the hsa module's population gate on the cap - a monthly coverage vector, an answered transfer month, an unmarried filer, and a transfer month in which the filer was an eligible individual - and it is argued there.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, WITH THE SECONDARY READ MFJ-GATED. The Switch default is False, each arm fences its filer fact with IsComplete, and the secondary arm additionally requires filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ, so a single-filer return - where /secondaryFiler has no item - resolves Complete false here rather than Incomplete. FALSE is also the adverse direction: it leaves ../isSupportedHfdElection on its unchanged conjunct (i) and ../hfdExclusionCap on the shipping ../hfdContributionLimit, so nothing about the cap can move a return that has not answered the transfer month.

Fact.Name: The ceiling ../line4cHfdExclusion is clamped to
Fact.Description:
The most of this form's HFD that may be excluded from income: the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) cap where it is computable, and ../hfdContributionLimit - Form 8889 line 3 plus line 7 - where it is not.
THE FALLBACK IS NOT A SECOND RULE, IT IS THE UNCHANGED ONE. Where the cap is not computable, conjunct (i) of ../isSupportedHfdElection still refuses any election whose filer total exceeds ../hfdContributionLimit, so on every form that reaches the clamp through that branch the elected amount is ALREADY at or under this figure and the LesserOf on ../line4cHfdExclusion is transparent. That is what keeps every committed case byte-identical: no committed fixture answers a transfer month, so ../hfdExclusionCapIsComputable is false on all of them and this fact is ../hfdContributionLimit exactly.
THE TWO FIGURES ARE THE SAME NUMBER for a filer whose coverage type did not change mid-year, since the (C)(i) substitution then substitutes the type the chart already carried. Where they differ - a self-only-to-family or family-to-self-only change - the statute names the transfer month's, and this fact is where that choice is made.
INCOMPLETE OUTSIDE THE FORM 8889 POPULATION in the fallback branch, inherited from ../hfdContributionLimit and harmless for its reason: ../isSupportedHfdElection tests IsComplete on that fact in its own Case before the conjunction, so a filer with no HSA contribution limit never reaches this clamp.

Fact.Name: This form's filer has also reported the HFD in the HSA section
Fact.Description:
Whether hsa:/filers/*/hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution is answered YES for the filer this form belongs to.
THIS IS A CONSISTENCY CONJUNCT, not a second intake. The HSA section already asks every filer with HSA contributions whether they made a qualified HSA funding distribution - the question is required for that section to be complete - so this return carries TWO statements about one event: the line-4c election here and that yes/no there. Requiring them to AGREE is what turns a double intake into a cross-check, and it is what lets hsa:/flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution narrow to the returns where they do not.
COMPLETE-SAFE AND FALSE BY DEFAULT. hsa:/filers/*/hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistributionDerived is Incomplete for a filer with no HSA contributions, so the IsComplete test comes first and the fallthrough is False. The polarity is deliberate: false means "the HSA section does not report an HFD for this filer", which is a REFUSAL of the exclusion, so a filer who was never asked the question cannot be excluded by silence.

Fact.Name: Box 3 checked on an HFD this dictionary can compute
Fact.Description:
The HFD elections whose printed treatment this dictionary produces. Every conjunct is doing work and each has its own refusal witness among the node tests, so a mis-wired one cannot hide behind a sibling. The shape is ../isSupportedQcdElection's, deliberately.
(a) BOX 3 IS CHECKED (../hasHfdElection, which is "hfd" in EITHER line 4c slot - ../line4cElection or ../line4cSecondElection), tested FIRST and in its own Case so the conjunction below is never evaluated - and never made Incomplete - on the forms that are not HFD elections. This conjunct is also half of the two-box pair test: ../hasUnsupportedLine4c Election refuses a form with a second box unless THIS fact and ../isSupportedQcdElection are both true.
(b) THE HFD AMOUNT IS ANSWERED, (c) THE BOX-3 DISCRIMINATOR IS ANSWERED and (d) THE FILER HAS AN HSA CONTRIBUTION LIMIT (../hfdContributionLimit is Complete). These three ride in a completeness Case above the All, so a missing answer refuses the election instead of making this fact Incomplete. (d) is not a formality: an HFD is a transfer INTO an HSA, so a filer whose return reports no HSA contributions has no limit for the transfer to fit inside and no Form 8889 Part I for it to appear on.
(e) THE AMOUNT IS NOT MORE THAN BOX 2a. "You can't exclude ... more than the amount that would otherwise be included in your income" is printed in the Exception itself and repeated in IRC 408(d)(9)(A) as "to the extent such distribution is otherwise includible in gross income". On the forms this arm admits box 2a is the whole distribution, so an amount above it is a contradictory answer rather than a capping situation, and it is refused rather than silently clamped - ../isSupportedQcdElection's conjunct (c) verbatim.
(f) BOX 2a EQUALS BOX 1 AND IS ABOVE $0. The HFD's signature on the form, and the same signature the QCD has: the custodian reports the distribution as fully taxable because it does not know where the money went. A form whose box 2a is BELOW box 1 has basis or another Exception in play, which is Exception 2's Form 8606 territory and is already refused by clause 1 of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution.
(g) THIS IS NOT THE ONE-TIME SPLIT-INTEREST-ENTITY QCD (../writableIsBox3SplitInterestEntityQcd answered false), which is the box-3 trap, argued on that fact.
(h) THE FILER HAS NOT USED THE LIFETIME ELECTION BEFORE (../hasNoPriorLifetimeHfdElection).
(i) THE FILER'S HFD TOTAL IS AT OR BELOW THE CONTRIBUTION LIMIT (../filerHfdTotal at or below ../hfdContributionLimit). The comparison is INCLUSIVE, because the printed rule is "can't exclude MORE THAN the limit", so a filer exactly at the limit is inside it. It is taken against the filer's TOTAL rather than this form's amount because the limit is per individual - the same per-taxpayer-versus-per-item reasoning ../isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling records - and above the limit the election is REFUSED rather than clamped, on that fact's precedent: clamping would need this dictionary to decide which part of a distribution stayed in income, which nothing printed here says. THAT SENTENCE IS NOT TRUE OF EVERY FILER, and the reason is worth recording. Something printed does say which part stays in income, and it is IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i): the exclusion "shall not exceed" the section 223(b) annual limitation computed on the coverage type in force at the time of the transfer, so the part above that limitation is the part that stays in income and Exception 4's own second sentence puts it on line 4b ("enter the part that isn\'t an HFD on line 4b"). What was missing was not a printed rule but the transfer MONTH, and that is now a intake (hsa:/filers/*/writableHsaFundingDistributionTransferMonth). The conjunct therefore now reads Any(at-or-under ../hfdContributionLimit, ../hfdExclusionCapIsComputable): where the cap is computable the election is SUPPORTED and ../line4cHfdExclusion clamps to ../hfdExclusionCap, and where it is not the conjunct is the unchanged refusal above. No committed case moves, because ../hfdExclusionCapIsComputable needs the new intake and no committed fixture answers it.
(j) THIS FORM IS THE FILER'S WHOLE HFD (../hfdElectedAmount equals ../filerHfdTotal). The election is once in a lifetime, so a filer with TWO HFD-electing forms in one year is claiming the printed exception - a second distribution in the same tax year after a self-only-to-family coverage change - and this landing REFUSES that exception rather than modelling it, because the intake it needs does not exist here: the exception turns on the coverage type held in the MONTH of each distribution, and the hsa module carries one coverage type per filer for the year. hsa:/flowKnockoutHsaSelfAndFamilyCoverage refuses a filer whose type is answered "both", which covers the mid-year change only if that is how the change is answered, and nothing here settles that - so the refusal is stated on its own ground rather than borrowed from that knockout. Stating it by dollars rather than by counting forms is ../isQcdOffsetAllocable's idiom.
(k) THE HSA SECTION REPORTS THE SAME HFD (../hsaSideReportsHfd). The two intakes for one event must agree; the conjunct is argued on that fact.
THE WITNESSES, one per conjunct that can fail on its own, so a mis-wired one cannot hide behind a sibling. Conjuncts (e) and (f) are ../isSupportedQcdElection's (c) and (d) verbatim and share their reasoning; (f)'s population is refused a second way by clause 1 of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution, so a form reaching it here is already knocked out.
NAMED, NOT FIXED - what this arm does NOT decide. The 12-month maintenance test and its consequences are Form 8889 Part III, and that is PARTLY MODELED: line 19, the funding-distribution income inclusion, and its 10% additional tax compute through hsa:/filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome and hsa:/filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax off a new per-filer intake, hsa:/filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth, which asks for the first month of the testing period in which the filer was not an eligible individual. What is left is line 18, the last-month-rule leg, refused by hsa:/flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes, and the case where that new question is unanswered on a return that has a line 10, refused by hsa:/flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution.
NEITHER CONDITION IS REPEATED HERE, still deliberately, and the reason is unchanged by the fill: they decide whether the return may be submitted, not what line 4b says, and duplicating them would give one refusal two reasons. The earlier wording of this paragraph said the guard "admits only a filer who was an eligible individual for the whole tax year"; that is no longer true and is corrected here.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 4b - the HSA funding distribution excluded from this IRA distribution
Fact.Description:
The part of this distribution that line 4b leaves out because it was transferred into the filer's HSA. $0 unless ../isSupportedHfdElection holds, and the elected amount when it does.
THE PRINTED RULE IS TWO SENTENCES AND THIS FACT IS BOTH OF THEM. "If the total amount distributed is an HFD and you elect to exclude it from income, enter -0- on line 4b" is this exclusion equalling box 2a; "If only part of the distribution is an HFD and you elect to exclude that part from income, enter the part that isn't an HFD on line 4b" is it being less. ../line4bTaxableAmount does the subtraction, so neither sentence is special-cased - the QCD half's shape, reached by the same reading.
NO REDUCTION TERM, unlike its QCD sibling. The QCD exclusion subtracts a post-70 1/2 contribution offset because section 219 deductions reduce the excludable amount; nothing printed reduces an HFD in the same way. What bounds it is the contribution limit, and that bound is a REFUSAL in ../isSupportedHfdElection rather than a subtraction here, so this fact is never negative and needs no clamp. THIS FACT CARRIES A CLAMP, THOUGH.
