The bound is still not a SUBTRACTION - the paragraph is right that nothing printed reduces an HFD - but it is a LesserOf against ../hfdExclusionCap, which is the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) ceiling where that is computable and the unchanged ../hfdContributionLimit where it is not. The clamp is what routes the uncapped part of a funding distribution to Form 1040 line 4b: ../line4bTaxableAmount subtracts this fact from box 2a, so an exclusion held at the cap leaves the overflow in the taxable amount with no new addend of any total anywhere. Exception 4's own second sentence is the printed authority - "enter the part that isn\'t an HFD on line 4b" - and IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) is what decides how large that part is. This fact is still never negative: the LesserOf can only lower it, and both operands are floored at $0.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT TOUCH IS LINE 4a, and that is not an omission. Exception 4 opens "enter the total distribution on line 4a", and income:/iraDistributions already carries the collection gross whenever the gross total differs from the line-4b total - a disjunct authored for Exception 1 that this Exception reaches for the same structural reason. So line 4a needs no term and gets none.
This fact is the HFD half of the former /form1099Rs/*/line4cQcdOrHfdExclusion.

Fact.Name: What this Form 1099-R contributes to Form 1040 line 4b
Fact.Description:
Box 2a less any QCD and any HFD excluded from it. This is the per-item term income:/taxableIraDistributionsFromForm1099Rs sums, and it exists because line 4b is summed in ANOTHER module: that fact was one rounded collection sum of box 2a, and on a QCD or an HFD box 2a equals box 1, so an exclusion computed in this module could not reach the line without a summand of its own.
TWO SUBTRAHENDS, AND THEY CAN BOTH BE POSITIVE ON ONE FORM. ../line4cQcdExclusion is $0 unless ../hasQcdElection and ../line4cHfdExclusion is $0 unless ../hasHfdElection - each through its own elected-amount fact and isSupported gate - and both of those predicates read EVERY line 4c slot - ../line4cElection, ../line4cSecondElection and ../line4cThirdElection - so a distribution carrying a QCD and an HFD subtracts both. That is what the printed instruction directs: check a box for each Exception and attach a statement showing the amount of each ("Line 4b - $1,000 Rollover and $500 HFD"); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 28. THE SUBTRACT STILL CANNOT OVER-SUBTRACT, and the reason is now each exclusion's own ceiling rather than an exclusivity between them: ../line4cQcdExclusion is capped at box 2a through ../isSupportedQcdElection's amount conditions and ../line4cHfdExclusion at the filer's HSA contribution limit and box 2a through ../isSupportedHfdElection's, and a pair whose two amounts together exceed box 2a fails those same conditions, so it is refused and this term is clamped to $0 rather than netted below zero. Any OTHER two-box combination - a rollover beside either, or the same option twice - is refused by ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection. The statement itself needs an attachment surface. This dictionary has no FREE-TEXT attachment idiom - the BOOLEAN one it does have is /writableForm5329Line54ReasonableCauseStatementAttached feeding /form5329Line54WaiverRequiresReasonableCauseStatement - and that absence, not a scope boundary, is why the statement is a named gap.
WHY NOT RE-BODY BOX 2a, which would need no new fact. ../taxableAmount has fourteen consumers in this module and one outside it, and they read it as THE REPORTED FIGURE rather than as a line-4b term: /primaryFiler1099RTaxableAmounts and /secondaryFiler1099RTaxableAmounts and their above-zero predicates, ../causesPreTaxToPostTaxRolloverKO's test against $0, the pension pair ../isTaxFreePensionRollover and ../isTaxablePensionRollover, ../isPartlyTaxablePension, ../isFullyTaxable, ../isDisabilityWagesBeforeMinRetirementAge, /taxableAmountsOfPartiallyTaxablePensions, both line-4c rollover arms, and clause 1 of ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution. Netting an exclusion into it would move all of them, and several are knockout inputs. The walk was re-run on this trunk rather than inherited.
NO ROUNDING OF ITS OWN, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT ALWAYS WHOLE DOLLARS. This paragraph used to claim it was ("../taxableAmount is already rounded and ../line4cQcdExclusion is bounded by it, so the difference is whole dollars"), and the first half is true while the conclusion is not: ../line4cQcdExclusion is built from ../qcdElectedAmount, which reads ../writableQcdAmount, an unrestricted Dollar carrying only a Min $0 Limit - and its other term, ../qcdPostSeventyContributionOffset, reads a second unrestricted Dollar the same way. A filer who answers a QCD of $5,000.40 against a rounded box 2a leaves a cents-valued term here. The BOUND is real - conjunct (c) of ../isSupportedQcdElection keeps the exclusion at or under box 2a, which is what "bounded by it" was about - but a bound is not a granularity.
THAT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, NOT A DEFECT, AND IT IS WHY THE CLAIM WAS CORRECTED RATHER THAN THE WRITABLE BOUNDED. Rounding on Form 1040 is optional and all-or-nothing for the filer ("You can round off cents to whole dollars on your return and schedules. If you do round to whole dollars, you must round all amounts"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23), and the printed line 4b is a TOTAL of per-distribution taxable amounts, so nothing printed requires this per-item term to be whole dollars. The single Round at the income-module total is preserved unchanged and is what settles line 4b - the round-once-at-the-total shape that module's siblings keep. Rounding here as well would round twice on the same money, which is the shape those siblings exist to avoid. (A whole-dollar granularity is not expressible as a Limit in any case - Limits are Min and Max.)
NEVER NEGATIVE, AND WITH TWO SUBTRAHENDS THE CLAMP IS WHAT HOLDS IT. The Subtract sits inside GreaterOf($0, ...). With one subtrahend the clamp could never bite - conjunct (c) of ../isSupportedQcdElection keeps a QCD exclusion at or under box 2a - but two exclusions each inside their own ceiling can still sum above box 2a, and that pair is refused by ../hasUnsupportedLine4cElection rather than netted: a $9,000 QCD beside a $4,000 HFD on a $12,000 distribution reads $0.00 here and at income:/taxableIraDistributions while /knockoutIraSepSimple refuses the return. The refusal is the substantive answer; the clamp keeps this per-item term itself from ever carrying a negative into a sum.

Fact.Name: Box 7 code 1 (under 59 1/2, no known exception) paired with a QCD election (70 1/2 or older)
Fact.Description:
A PAYER/FILER CONTRADICTION, on the same shape as form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/box9aMrdBox8ContradictionRefusesThisReturn: two assertions on one Form 1099-R that cannot both be true, so this fact names the conflict rather than picking a side, and the return-level knockout beside it refuses instead.
THE TWO ASSERTIONS. Box 7 code 1's own printed Explanation is "Use Code 1 only if the participant has not reached age 59 1/2, and you do not know if any of the exceptions under Code 2, 3, or 4 apply" - the PAYER's statement that the recipient is under 59 1/2. IRC 408(d)(8)(B)(ii) defines a qualified charitable distribution as one "made on or after the date that the individual for whose benefit the plan is maintained has attained age 70 1/2" - the FILER's own election, by making it, asserting they cleared a bar nine years past the one the payer's code admits. A recipient cannot be both under 59 1/2 and at least 70 1/2, so a code-1 form on which the filer also elects a QCD (../hasQcdElection - the box checked in EITHER line 4c slot) carries both assertions at once, and nothing on the return says which one is wrong.
THE CODE FAMILY. Bare "1", and every lawful code-1 companion pair in both digit orders, per Table 1's own *Used with code* column for the code-1 row: "8, B, D, K, L, M, or P" - 18/81, 1B/B1, 1D/D1, 1K/K1, 1L/L1, 1M/M1, 1P/P1. Each of these fifteen spellings carries code 1's own under-59 1/2 assertion; the companion only adds a SECOND fact about the same distribution (a return of excess contributions, a designated Roth account, an IRA whose FMV is unavailable, a loan, a qualified plan loan offset, or a prior-year excess), never a different age. ../isLawfulDistributionCodePair is this dictionary's own list of the pairs Table 1 blesses; every code-1 spelling here is drawn from it, not invented.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: IsComplete on ../distributionCode (Incomplete on an unanswered box 7 - ../distributionCode's own Derived has no fallback Case) and on ../line4cElection (never actually Incomplete, per that fact's own Description, but wrapped anyway on the same footing as the box9a precedent) both come before the value reads that follow them, so an unanswered form and a no-1099-R return both resolve FALSE rather than leaking an Incomplete.
WHAT THIS CATCHES THAT NOTHING CAUGHT BEFORE. ../isQcdEligibleByAge tests the filer's DOB against ../isQcdEligibleByAge's bound; ../isSupportedQcdElection reads it, but nothing here reads box 7. A code-1 form whose filer's OWN DOB clears the QCD age bound - so the QCD computes and the return files - is exactly the shape this fact now catches: the payer's code and the filer's own DOB disagree about the same recipient's age, and disagreeing sources are refused rather than adjudicated by trusting one over the other, the same principle box9a's payer-side contradiction rests on. THIS IS NOT A HYPOTHETICAL POPULATION: a code 1 form with a QCD of $8,000 and a date of birth of 1953-06-15 is precisely this shape. No narrower reading of this contradiction spares that fixture without also sparing the bug it names: its own facts (code 1, QCD elected, both complete) are exactly this guard's population. Its /flowIsKnockedOut line is re-measured Complete true in this fill (was Placeholder false) - the only line that moves; every arithmetic assert on it is untouched.

Fact.Name: This form carries a line 4c election this dictionary cannot honour
Fact.Description:
True when the filer has checked a line-4c box whose printed treatment this dictionary does not compute. THAT IS NO LONGER A WHOLE BOX. This sentence used to read "at this landing that is EVERY answered election", which three successive landings have falsified, and it is corrected here rather than carried because a reader meets it before the paragraphs that qualify it. What is refused TODAY: under box 1, an INDIRECT rollover the filer did not separately indicate and a direct rollover whose box 2a is the whole of box 1; under box 2, a QCD election failing any conjunct of ../isSupportedQcdElection; and under box 3, an HFD election failing any conjunct of ../isSupportedHfdElection. No box is refused whole any more. What IS refused whole is a THIRD box on one distribution, for the reason the third-slot paragraph below gives. The per-box reasons below are kept because they are the argument, not the summary.
QCD (box 2, Exception 3) NO LONGER FALLS HERE AS A CLASS. The QCD half of the residue was built as the successor to the contract named below, so a QCD election that satisfies ../isSupportedQcdElection is carved out by the SECOND Case alongside the two rollover arms; the first Case is the two-box pair test above it. Both of Exception 3's printed sentences compute. What is still refused under box 2 is every conjunct that fact names: no QCD amount answered, an amount above box 2a, a box 2a below box 1, a recipient this dictionary cannot place at age 70 1/2 for the whole year, a per-filer QCD total above the annual ceiling, a current-year traditional IRA contribution that would offset the exclusion, the one-time split-interest-entity election, an unstated post-70 1/2 IRA deduction history, and a stated history on a filer whose QCD is split across more than one form (where nothing printed says which form's exclusion is cut). THE TWO PARAGRAPHS THAT USED TO STAND HERE ARE KEPT BELOW IN THE PAST TENSE, because they were the reasons and one of them was wrong. (a) The exclusion has printed CEILINGS - a total of $108,000 of QCDs for the year, including up to $54,000 for a one-time QCD to a split-interest entity, with the same rules applying separately to a spouse on a joint return. Those are indexed tax parameters, and this dictionary's rule is that a nonzero dollar literal carries a row in the authority parameter ledger; that ground was CORRECT and was discharged by writing the row (authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv, qcd-annual-exclusion-limit) rather than by waiving it, and the $54,000 figure turned out not to be owed at all because the split-interest-entity election is refused outright. (b) The age condition is "You must have been at least age 70 1/2 when the distribution was made", and no fact in this dictionary carries the DATE of a Form 1099-R distribution, so the condition cannot be decided in general from a date of birth alone - a filer who turns 70 1/2 mid-year qualifies for a December distribution and not for a March one. Refusing above the ceiling would need the same literal as modeling below it, so there is no ceiling-free half to land.
HFD (box 3, Exception 4) NO LONGER FALLS HERE AS A CLASS EITHER, and the paragraph that used to stand here is kept below in the past tense because it was the reason and it did not survive. It read: the exclusion is bounded by the HSA contribution limit and reported through Form 8889 Part III, and it is once in a lifetime - "you can generally elect to exclude an HFD from your income once in your lifetime" - with a maintenance test over the 12 months following that can claw the exclusion back, and none of that is representable from a single tax year's Form 1099-R. Three of those four turned out to be buildable and the fourth turned out to belong somewhere else. The HSA contribution limit is Form 8889 line 3 plus line 7, which ../hfdContributionLimit reads per filer. Form 8889 line 10 is now the computed HFD total rather than a $0 constant (hsa:/filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionsTotal), so the contribution room the transfer consumes is reported where the form reports it. The lifetime rule is a per-filer attestation whose silence is a refusal, which the BUILD-FIRST directive licenses. What was left is Form 8889 PART III, the 12-month maintenance test, and it is not this predicate's to answer: it decides whether the return may be SUBMITTED rather than what line 4b says, so it stayed on hsa:/flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution. THAT SENTENCE ORIGINALLY ENDED "which now admits only a filer who was an eligible individual for the whole tax year", AND THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE: the hsa-testing-period fill built Part III line 19 off a new per-filer intake, hsa:/filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth, so a filer who was not eligible all year and answers that question computes. The guard now admits that filer too and refuses only the two missing-input cases named on hsa:/filers/*/hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution. What is still refused under box 3 is every conjunct ../isSupportedHfdElection names: no HFD amount answered, an amount above box 2a, a box 2a below box 1, the box-3 split-interest-entity QCD, an unstated or spent lifetime election, a filer whose HFD total is above their HSA contribution limit, a filer with more than one HFD-electing form, and a filer whose HSA section does not report the same transfer. THE SIXTH ITEM IN THAT LIST IS NARROWED, though, and is no longer "a filer whose HFD total is above their HSA contribution limit" whole. Conjunct (i) is Any(at-or-under ../hfdContributionLimit, ../hfdExclusionCapIsComputable), so a filer over the limit whose IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) cap IS computable - monthly coverage vector answered, transfer month answered, unmarried, transfer month an eligible non-Medicare month - is SUPPORTED, and ../line4cHfdExclusion clamps to the cap instead of collapsing to $0. What is still refused under that item is the filer over the limit whose cap is NOT computable. Nothing else in this list moves.
THE QCD REFUSAL WAS RE-DERIVED AND DID NOT SURVIVE, AND THE HFD ONE FOLLOWED IT. The record is kept here because the two paragraphs above read as a roadmap and that roadmap has now been walked end to end. What the QCD half actually needed was three things and none of them was a wait: the ceiling's ledger row, which this landing wrote; a per-item QCD amount, because a QCD is invisible on the form and a PARTIAL one is indistinguishable from a full one, which this landing intakes; and a line-4b term in the income module, because that line is a collection sum of box 2a and box 2a equals box 1 on a QCD, which ../line4bTaxableAmount supplies. The age condition never was the operative ground: a SUFFICIENT date-of-birth bound decides the cohort that was old enough all year with no intake at all, and ../isQcdEligibleByAge takes that route, at born-on-or-before 1954-06-30 - a bound that holds under the day count AND under the six calendar months, so it needs no convention, which matters because that convention is printed in NO source vendored here (searched: the Form 1040 instructions, Pub 590-A, Pub 590-B and IRC 408 all use "age 70 1/2" undefined).
WHAT THE HFD HALF NEEDED WAS THE HSA MODULE. Its own contract named one live ground and it was real: hsa:/filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionsTotal was a $0 constant carrying an mef Export and it IS Form 8889 line 10, so an HFD excluded from income while line 10 reported zero would have over-stated the contribution room and the Part I deduction - a contradiction inside one return, in the taxpayer-favourable direction, and one no shape confined to this module could repair. The fill that repaired it did so in one commit by landing both sides, and found a second ground the contract had missed: the HSA module already refused every reported HFD outright, so the exclusion and that knockout had to move together.
ROLLOVER (box 1, Exception 1) is the one box with a computable treatment, and BOTH of Exception 1's printed branches are now CARVED OUT rather than refused: the SECOND Case is an Any of ../isFullDirectRolloverElection (the total distribution rolled over, box 2a $0, line 4b -0-) and ../isPartialDirectRolloverElection (part rolled over, $0 below box 2a below box 1, line 4b the part not rolled over). The partial half needs no intake because inside Exception 1's scope box 2a IS the part not rolled over, which ../isPartialDirectRolloverElection derives.
What is STILL refused under box 1: an INDIRECT rollover the filer did not separately indicate (see ../isFullDirectRolloverElection for why that half is left to /flowKnockoutForRollover), and a direct rollover whose box 2a is the whole of box 1, which Exception 1 does not reach because nothing was rolled over.
NOT A SECOND REASON for a refusal that already fires elsewhere in the ordinary case: this predicate is read from ../isUnsupportedIraDistribution AFTER that Switch's box-2a-differs and direct-rollover clauses, so a form those clauses already refuse never reaches it. It DOES overlap /flowKnockoutForRollover for one shape - a code 1/2/3/7 form on which the filer answered ../writableIsIndirectRollover true AND checked box 1 - and no double-intake refusal in the /knockoutIraDistributionDoubleIntake style is owed for that overlap, because both paths land on REFUSED and so cannot produce contradictory numbers. That overlap is pinned by a fixture rather than reasoned, which is this module's own convention for a "covered elsewhere" claim.
Complete false whenever ALL THREE line 4c slots are "none", which is every unanswered form and every non-IRA form.
THE THIRD SLOT IS TESTED FIRST OF ALL, and it is a flat refusal: when ../line4cThirdElection is anything but "none" this fact is TRUE, because there is no supported triple. The only combination beyond a single box that computes is a QCD in one slot and an HFD in another, so a third box always puts a rollover beside an exclusion, and that pair is refused by the Case below. The slot exists so that a filer to whom three Exceptions apply can SAY so and be refused, instead of entering the two that compute and filing a return that silently drops the third and over-states line 4b by its amount. Three slots is also all the printed row can hold: line 4c prints exactly three boxes.
THE SECOND SLOT IS TESTED NEXT, before the supported-election Any below. ONE SHAPE HAS SINCE BEEN LIFTED OUT of this clause by the carve-out above it, and only one: an ELECTED partial DIRECT rollover, where the filer has told the return on line 4c box 1 which Exception applies and Exception 1's own scope makes box 2a the part not rolled over. [CORRECTION: this sentence named /knockoutTaxablePensionRollover, which no longer exists. The claim is unchanged and is if anything stronger now: what still holds an IRA-flagged G/H form with a positive box 2a is the NARROWED /flowKnockoutForPreTaxToPostTaxRollover plus this clause.] Without this clause a code-G IRA rollover would fall through to the new collection route and be reported as an ordinary taxable distribution. Fact.Name: This Form 1099-R belongs in the Form 8880 line 4 distribution total
Fact.Description:
Whether box 1 of this form is one of the distributions Form 8880 line 4 adds up. The printed rule is an inclusion of every distribution from an IRA, a 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457(b), 501(c)(18)(D), SEP, SIMPLE or TSP account or a section 4974(c) qualified plan, less a closed list of exclusions. So the test is: box 7 carries at least one code that reports such a distribution, and no code that marks an excluded one.
CODES THAT PUT THE FORM IN: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, B, J, K, M, Q, S and T, and A or Y beside them. Each is a distribution from one of the listed plan types. Code 3 (disability) is in even when the payment goes to Form 1040 line 1h as wages, because line 4 counts distributions received, not the line they are taxed on. Code M (a qualified plan loan offset) is an actual distribution and is not the deemed loan distribution of code L.
CODES THAT KEEP THE FORM OUT, whatever else box 7 carries: 6 (a section 1035 exchange) and 9 (the cost of current life insurance protection) are not distributions from the account; 8, P and E are the returned excess contributions and deferrals the fifth and sixth bullets exclude; C (a life insurance death benefit), D (a nonqualified annuity) and F (a charitable gift annuity) are not from any listed plan type; G and H are direct rollovers; L is a loan treated as a distribution; N and R are recharacterizations; U is section 404(k) ESOP dividends; W is a long-term care charge against an annuity.
TWO EXCLUSIONS NEED MORE THAN THE CODE. A code 4 form with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked is an inherited IRA, and the last bullet excludes it when the beneficiary is not the spouse. The form does not say which, so an IRA code 4 form is kept out. A spouse beneficiary who keeps the IRA as an inherited IRA is therefore under-counted. A traditional IRA distribution converted to a Roth IRA is excluded through ../writableConvertedToRothIra. The military retirement plan bullet stays on the two filters that read this fact. The portion of a distribution rolled over within 60 days is not taken out here: box 1 is counted whole.

Incomplete, with no default, while any answered form cannot yet be classified (for example a Simplified Method form whose taxable amount is held), so line 5a never omits a pension it cannot place.
THE True CATCH-ALL IS GONE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CHANGE. This fact used to carry a two-arm Switch - the IsComplete-plus-nonempty arm that is now arm 2, then a True arm returning $0 - so a return whose only Form 1099-R could not be classified fell through to that default and PRINTED $0 on line 5a beside a distribution the filer certainly received. The undecidable operand is ../isPartlyTaxablePension, whose Not(Equal(../grossDistribution, form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount)) cannot be decided while the effective taxable amount is held; /form1099RsWithPartlyTaxablePension is then Incomplete, arm 2's IsComplete is false, and a True arm sitting after an undecidable guard is TAKEN rather than skipped. The body is now the same three-arm shape the two line 5b addends /fullyTaxablePensions and /taxableAmountsOfPartiallyTaxablePensions already carry, whose own Descriptions state the rule this one was missing, so the disclosure line and the taxable line hold together instead of one defaulting while the other refuses.
WHAT MOVES AND WHAT DOES NOT. Arm 1 keeps the $0 that a return with an unanswered Form 1099-R collection resolved before. Arm 2 is the old first arm verbatim, so every return that classified its forms and summed them resolves the same figure. Arm 3 keeps the $0 for a return whose forms are all classified and none partly taxable. Only the middle state - collection answered, classification undecided - changes, and on every such return /fullyTaxablePensions was ALREADY Incomplete for the same reason, because ../isFullyTaxable and ../isPartlyTaxablePension partition on the same box 1 versus effective-taxable-amount equality. Line 5b, /totalIncome and the tax were therefore already held on exactly this population: the change is to what line 5a PRINTS on a held return, never to a filed figure.

The sum of gross distributions on the Forms 1099-R that are fully taxable pensions (box 2a equal to box 1), one of the two addends of Form 1040 line 5b. $0 when the Form 1099-R collection is unanswered or when no form is a fully taxable pension. Incomplete, with no default, while any answered form cannot yet be classified (for example a Simplified Method form whose taxable amount is held), so line 5b never omits a pension it cannot place.

The sum of the effective taxable amounts on the Forms 1099-R that are partly taxable pensions (taxable amount below box 1), one of the two addends of Form 1040 line 5b. $0 when the Form 1099-R collection is unanswered or when no form is a partly taxable pension. Incomplete, with no default, while any answered form cannot yet be classified (for example a Simplified Method form whose taxable amount is held), so line 5b never omits a pension it cannot place.

Fact.Name: The part of this Form 1099-R that Form 8958 line 7 can allocate
Fact.Description:
THE CEILING AND THE BASE, in one fact: exactly this form's own contribution to Form 1040 line 5b, and $0 for every form that contributes nothing to it.
THE IDENTITY THIS FACT IS BUILT ON, verified against the bodies rather than assumed. income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities is /fullyTaxablePensions plus /taxableAmountsOfPartiallyTaxablePensions less /psoPremiumExclusion. The first sums ../grossDistribution over /form1099RsWithFullyTaxablePension, whose filter is ../isFullyTaxable — which REQUIRES ../grossDistribution to equal form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount. The second sums form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount over /form1099RsWithPartlyTaxablePension, whose filter is ../isPartlyTaxablePension. The two filters partition ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension on that same equality, so the sum of this fact over the collection is AT MOST the line 5b minuend - and exactly equal when no IRA form satisfies the pension predicate (this fact's own ../notIraSepSimple conjunct narrows it; the bound direction is what the adjustment needs).
WHY effectiveTaxableAmount AND NOT BOX 2a. Box 2a is the amount the PAYER reported; effectiveTaxableAmount is the amount this return actually includes after the supported elections and worksheets, and those two part company on real shapes — an INDIRECT ROLLOVER reports a box 2a of $20,000 and includes $2,000, so halving box 2a would subtract $10,000 from a $2,000 line. It also buys a printed rule for free: Publication 555 says that for the Form 4972 ten year tax option "you must disregard community" property laws (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 6, LEFT column of a two column extraction), and effectiveTaxableAmount is $0 on a form with the Form 4972 inputs complete, so such a form's allocable base is $0 and no community property law touches it. That is structural, not a special case.
THE IRA CONJUNCT IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE CONJUNCT IN THIS UNIT THAT NO FIXTURE WITNESSES. ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension is already a pension side predicate, so removing ../notIraSepSimple moves no test — measured, not assumed: mutation M3 of this unit's sweep deleted it and 134 of 134 cases stayed green. It ships anyway, and the rule that admits it is stated here because the SAME fill REFUSED an unwitnessable conjunct one module over (form1099Misc's guard was left byte-identical for exactly that reason). THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE. This conjunct can only ever REFUSE MORE — if ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension were widened tomorrow to admit an IRA form, this conjunct keeps the allocable base at $0 and the return keeps refusing. The 1099-MISC conjunct would have REFUSED LESS: it sits inside a Not() on a shipping knockout, so an unwitnessed version of it could only ever lift a refusal. An unwitnessed conjunct that can only fail closed is cheap insurance; an unwitnessed conjunct that can only fail open is the defect.
PART-II-ONLY FORM 4972 FORMS NOW ENTER THIS BASE. Everything above is kept unedited and ONE claim in it is now conditional: the Form 4972 sentence read that effectiveTaxableAmount is $0 on a Form 4972 form, so its allocable base is $0 and no community property law reaches it. That is TRUE FOR PART III ONLY. Pub. 555 disregards community property laws for the 10-YEAR TAX OPTION - "For the 10-year tax option, you must disregard community" / "property laws." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 6, the LEFT column of a two-column extraction) - and a Part-II-only election is the 20 percent CAPITAL GAIN election, not the 10-year option. So a Part-II-only form's ordinary income portion entering this base is the CORRECT reading of that same sentence, not a gap; a Part III form still fails ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension and still contributes $0 here. Structural, as before.

Fact.Name: (Writable) How much of this pension's taxable amount is community income?
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM CHARACTER INPUT, and it is a DOLLAR rather than the Boolean the wages and interest rows of this class use. That divergence is compelled by the source, not chosen for expressiveness, and the IRS's own worked example is what compels it.
WHAT THE SOURCES SAY. Form 8958 characterises wages with no state law qualifier — they "are community income and must be evenly split." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3) — but for pensions it states a PERIOD rule and then declines to fix it. The rule, taken as SEVEN consecutive lines of the RIGHT column of a two column extraction and quoted one line at a time because a downward read of the whole line produces text the document does not contain (correction #5): "Pensions. Generally, distributions from pensions will be" (line 101) / "characterized as community or separate income depending on the" (102) / "respective periods of participation in the pension while married (or" (103) / "during the registered domestic partnership) and domiciled in a" (104) / "community property state or in a noncommunity property state" (105) / "during the total period of participation in the pension. These rules" (106) / "may vary between states." (107); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf. Publication 555 prints the same rule at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 5 RIGHT column and 349-351 LEFT column (page break at 348), and adds "states. Check your state law." (line 351). Line 7's own instruction says only to "allocate the total from column A between each spouse or RDP in columns B and C" (same file, lines 173-174) — no ratio at all.
WHY NOT A BOOLEAN, AND WHY NOT A PERIODS INTAKE. Publication 555's Henry Wright example is a PARTLY community pension: 30 years of civil service, 15 of them married and domiciled in a community property state, so "erty state, half the civil service retirement pay is consid-" / "ered to be community income." and, of a $1,000 monthly payment, "$1,000 a month in retirement pay, $500 is considered" / "community income—half ($250) is his income and half" / "($250) is his spouse's." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 6, LEFT column of a two column extraction, read DOWN the left column). A Boolean cannot say that; it can only say "all" or "none", and either answer files a wrong number on the IRS's own example. A months of participation intake could say it, but it would EMBED the CP months over total months proration as a rule of this dictionary — and that is precisely the rule the form says "may vary between states". A dollar portion asks the filer for the conclusion their state's law gives them and embeds no rule. The attested per form dollar is an idiom this module already uses where a determination is the taxpayer's: ../writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain is the precedent.
WHAT IS BEING ASKED FOR, precisely, because the wording is the whole safety of the fact: the community share OF THE TAXABLE AMOUNT this form puts on Form 1040 line 5b — not of box 1, and not of a fraction. ../communityIncomePortion clamps the answer into [$0, this form's line 5b contribution]; the clamp is a backstop against a mis-scaled answer, never a reinterpretation of the question.
NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY. Unanswered is $0 allocated, which leaves the whole distribution on this return (the status quo) and leaves ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refusing when the form is the spouse's. Fail closed; this dictionary never assumes community.

Fact.Name: The community part of this pension's taxable amount
Fact.Description:
../writableCommunityIncomePortion read complete safe and clamped into [$0, ../communityAllocablePensionBase]. IsComplete FIRST, so an unanswered portion resolves $0 rather than Incomplete: nothing downstream may be dragged Incomplete by a question nobody has been asked yet, and $0 is the fail closed direction.
THE CLAMP IS TWO SIDED AND BOTH SIDES ARE DELIBERATE. A negative answer cannot subtract income from this return; an answer above this form's own line 5b contribution cannot allocate more than the form contributes, which is what keeps the return level adjustment from ever exceeding the line it adjusts.
THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not re-proposed: refusing the return when the answer exceeds the base, as an input contradiction. Rejected because a new refusal is not needed for a case the clamp already handles conservatively, and because every return this fact can be non zero on is refused anyway by filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws.

Fact.Name: This pension is community income in its entirety
Fact.Description:
A POSITIVE allocable base, all of which the filer has characterised as community income. Both conjuncts are load bearing and the FIRST is the sharp one: without the greater than $0 test, a form whose base is $0 — every IRA form, every Form 4972 form, every form that reaches no Form 1040 line — would satisfy "portion equals base" as $0 equals $0 and read WHOLLY COMMUNITY. That is not an aesthetic defect: this fact is the third conjunct of ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, so it would narrow the guard for a spouse's IRA distribution, whose amount sits in the UNSCOPED line 4a/4b sums that this unit does not adjust at all.
WHY THE GUARD NEEDS "WHOLLY" AND NOT MERELY "SOME", which is the other half of the same argument and is an arithmetic one. The return level adjustment is MINUS the sum of the halves. On the taxpayer's OWN partly community pension that is exactly right — a $12,000 pension with $6,000 of community income leaves $6,000 separate (all of it this filer's) plus $3,000, i.e. $9,000, which is the Wright example's answer. On the SPOUSE's partly community pension it is not: the spouse's separate half belongs on the spouse's return in full and would have to leave this one entirely. So a spouse's form is lifted out of the guard only when it is wholly community, where the two formulas coincide.

Fact.Name: This form's community-property character question is owed and unanswered
Fact.Description: TRUE when this form has a POSITIVE allocable base and ../writableCommunityIncomePortion has no answer. BOTH CONJUNCTS ARE LOAD-BEARING, and the base test is the carve the sibling Boolean collections do not need: an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE form and a Form 4972 form have a $0 base because the law itself settles their character (an IRA is deemed separate property), so no answer is OWED on them and an unanswered portion there must not keep filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete false forever. On a positive-base form the unanswered portion is a real gap: the item allocates $0 and stays whole on this return, which on an allocation return may be the wrong figure, so the gap must be VISIBLE at the return level rather than silently defaulted. This fact changes no figure. Read only by /form1099Rs/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete.

Fact.Name: Some Form 1099-R community-property character is owed and unanswered
Fact.Description: GreaterThan(Count of per-item owed-and-unanswered characters, 0), the same return-level shape as /form1099Rs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ. Read by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete, whose IsComplete-first wrapper is what keeps filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws complete-safe when this collection is absent: an absent root is Placeholder on the JVM, the wrapper reads that as NOT complete, and the refusal stands. Fail closed.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 7 — the crossing half of this payer's community pension (not the column B figure)
Fact.Description:
Half of the community part of ONE Form 1099-R's taxable amount, on a return that must allocate community income. $0 on every other return, and $0 on any form whose community portion is $0 — which includes every unanswered form, every IRA form and every form that reaches no Form 1040 line.
THE HALF IS PRINTED AND THE PORTION IS NOT. Once an amount IS community income, Form 8958's operative sentence fixes the split at a half ("You must report half of all community income and all of your" separate income, line 124), and Publication 555's Wright example applies exactly that arithmetic to a pension: of the $500 a month that is community income, "community income—half ($250) is his income and half" / "($250) is his spouse's." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 6, LEFT column of a two column extraction). What no source fixes is HOW MUCH of the distribution is community, which is why the portion is an intake and the half is a Rational.
ROUNDED AT THE DOLLAR, PER FORM, AND THAT IS THIS MODULE'S CONVENTION RATHER THAN A CHOICE MADE HERE. Every per form income amount in this module is already Round wrapped at the form — ../grossDistribution and ../taxableAmount both are — so income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities, Form 1040 line 5b, carries no Round of its own and has been whole dollars by construction since the L0 import. A cents bearing addend would put cents on that printed line for the first time, on a line that is also exported to the state systems. The allocation therefore rounds where the module rounds. The WITHHOLDING twin below does the OPPOSITE, for the same reason read the other way: /form1099RsFederalIncomeTaxWithheld deliberately hands CENTS upward to Form 1040 line 25b, so its allocation must too.
THE ROUNDING MODE IS HALF UP, AND IT IS NOT THE MODE THE WAGES ROW OF THIS CLASS MEASURED. These are different operators at different scales, and the difference was measured rather than carried over. A first draft of this Description asserted HALF EVEN at the dollar and the fixture refuted it (records state what IS). TWO BOUNDED CONSEQUENCES, disclosed rather than smoothed. (i) On an odd dollar portion the two spouses' halves total a dollar more or less than column A, a miss against the form's own footing rule "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction). (ii) The return level total can differ from half of the whole by up to half a dollar per payer. Neither is fixable inside the dictionary: the rounding mode is engine behaviour.
IT CAN NEVER EXCEED THE FORM'S OWN CONTRIBUTION TO LINE 5b even after rounding up: a base of $B allocates at most $(B+1)/2, which is at most $B for every $B of a dollar or more, and a base below a dollar allocates $0 or $1 against a base this module has already rounded to a whole dollar, so the only equality case is $B = $1.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 11 — the crossing half of this payer's box 4 (not the column B figure)
Fact.Description:
Half of ONE Form 1099-R's box 4 federal income tax withheld, on a WHOLLY community pension on an allocation return, because the credit follows the income it was withheld from. $0 everywhere else. Cents preserved; Form 1040 line 25b rounds once at its own line.
WHOLLY COMMUNITY ONLY, AND THE GAP IS NAMED RATHER THAN FILLED. On a PARTLY community pension the printed sources fix no ratio for the withholding at all: Form 8958 line 11's instruction says to allocate without stating one, and the printed half appears only in the form's community WAGES paragraph ("each of you is entitled to credit for half the income tax withheld on", line 182). Prorating box 4 by portion over base would invent exactly the kind of arithmetic this contract exists to refuse. So a partly community pension keeps 100% of its credit on this return while reporting less than 100% of its income — an OVER CREDIT, i.e. taxpayer favourable, which is the direction that would matter if such a return could file. It cannot: filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws refuses every return this fact can be non zero on. This is a standing gap.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated pension income (Form 8958 line 7)
Fact.Description:
THE CONTRACT PATH. Half the community part of every allocable pension on this return, totalled over every payer. Whole dollars: the per payer halves are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once here.
WHAT THIS FIGURE IS, STATED CAREFULLY, because it is NOT always the column B entry of Form 8958 line 7. It is HALF THE COMMUNITY PORTION — the amount that CROSSES between the two returns. On a WHOLLY community pension that equals column B, since half the community part is also half of column A. On a PARTLY community pension of the taxpayer's own it does not: the Wright example's column B is $9,000 of a $12,000 annuity ($6,000 separate plus half of the $6,000 that is community), while this fact reports the $3,000 that crosses. The crossing figure is the one the printed line moves by, which is why it is the one this fact carries and why /communityPropertyPensionAllocationAdjustment is its exact negation.
$0 on every return the gate reads false on, which is every ordinary return.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated pension withholding (Form 8958 line 11, 1099-R leg)
Fact.Description:
The column B/C figure of Form 8958 line 11 for Form 1099-R box 4 only: half the federal income tax withheld on the wholly community pensions this return reports half of. Whole dollars, rounded once here over cents bearing addends.
IT IS A LEG, NOT THE LINE. Form 8958 line 11 covers every payer's withholding; the wage leg is formW2s:/communityPropertyAllocatedFederalWithholding. The remaining Form 1040 line 25b legs are not allocated by this unit and are named gaps.

Fact.Name: The community pension half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
A NEGATIVE, cents bearing addend: MINUS the sum of the per payer community halves. It is an addend of income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities, Form 1040 line 5b.
WHY THE NEGATION AND NOT THE WAGES ROW'S FORMULA. formW2s:/communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded is allocated MINUS unscoped, which is right only because EVERY W-2 is community income. This collection is MIXED by construction — an IRA form, an unanswered form and a partly community form all sit in it — and on a mixed collection that formula deletes the filer's own separate income from the printed line. The negation is the same correction the interest and dividends row of this class had to make, and it degenerates to the wages formula exactly when every form is wholly community.
IT CANNOT EXCEED THE LINE IT ADJUSTS, and that is structural rather than tested: each addend is half of a portion that ../communityIncomePortion clamps to that form's own line 5b contribution, and the sum of those contributions IS the line 5b minuend (the identity is argued on ../communityAllocablePensionBase). So the adjusted line is at worst the minuend halved.
ONE RESIDUAL, NAMED: income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities also SUBTRACTS /psoPremiumExclusion, which this fact knows nothing about, so a retired public safety officer electing the premium exclusion on a wholly community pension can drive line 5b below zero when the exclusion exceeds the unallocated half. The exclusion is capped at $3,000 per filer and the population is a community property allocation return, every one of which is refused by filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws, so nothing files. Halving the exclusion was considered and rejected: IRC 402(l) is a personal election of the retired officer, not an item of community income, and no source splits it.
NO GATE ON THIS FACT, deliberately: every addend of the CollectionSum is already $0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, so this fact is $0 there too.
LINE 5a IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADJUSTED. income:/pensionsAndAnnuities is NOT the collection's gross — it is tax free rollovers plus PARTLY taxable gross plus two carve out grosses — so an unconditional negative addend there could exceed its own base and print a negative line 5a on a return carrying one ordinary fully taxable pension, whose contribution to that line is $0. Leaving 5a whole OVER states the disclosure line, which is the conservative direction, and 5a feeds no computation: income:/totalIncome takes line 5b. This is a standing gap.

Fact.Name: The pension withholding half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
The Form 1040 line 25b twin of /communityPropertyPensionAllocationAdjustment: a negative, cents bearing addend equal to MINUS the sum of the per payer withholding halves. It is an addend of /form1099RsFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, which is itself one term of line 25b, so the credit is netted where the income is and no other module is touched.
$0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, and $0 on every form that is not wholly community, by the addends themselves.

Fact.Name: Percentage for 1099-R box 8
Fact.Description: Percentage. Form 1099-R box 8 (Other, percentage).

Fact.Name: Box 8 percentage as an integer number of thousandths of a percent
Fact.Description:
THE NUMERIC BOX 8 DIVISOR, the number that /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage needs. ../writableOtherPercentage above is a Writable String carrying the MeF RatioType Match limit, and this fact graph has no string-to-number operator, so the divisor Form 4972's multiple-recipient procedure needs for LINE 11 has to be DECLARED rather than derived. This is the box 8 twin of the shipping ../writableBox9aPercentageThousandths and is built to the same convention for the same two measured reasons that fact's Description records: the limits registry has no granularity type, and a Rational intake could not close the tie two ways under AsDecimalString's HALF_UP setScale. An integer number of thousandths over 1000 is a Rational at exactly thousandths granularity BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what lets form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/box8DivisorTiesToMefString hold in BOTH directions.
IT IS NOT THE BOX 9a PERCENTAGE, and that distinction is the whole reason a second intake exists. Form 4972's multiple-recipient Step 2 divides box 2a by the BOX 9a percentage onto line 8 and box 8 by the BOX 8 percentage onto line 11, in the same step and in adjacent bullets (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 3). Two divisors, two dividends, one step.
THE UNIT IS THOUSANDTHS OF A PERCENT: 50 percent is 50000, 12.345 percent is 12345, 100 percent is 100000 and that is the Max. The Match limit on the String admits at most three decimal places, so no legal String spelling is finer than this intake. NOT a MeF value - the String above is what is transmitted; this intake exists only so the engine can divide.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION, under the project owner's directive that a writable's own Description must let the application build the screen without opening an IRS document.
THIS IS NOT A QUESTION TO THE FILER. It is a DERIVATION the application performs on an answer it already holds, and no new screen appears. The filer has already been asked, and has already answered, ../writableOtherPercentage - "Percentage" on the Form 1099-R box 8 entry screen, the MeF RatioType String. The application sends this fact as that same number re-expressed as an integer count of thousandths of a percent. If the application ever chooses to surface it, the question text is "Box 8 percentage, in thousandths of a percent" and it is a display of a computed value, not an input.
THE DERIVATION, exactly. Take the answered String, which the Match limit ^100(\.0{1,3})?|[0-9]{1,2}(\.\d{1,3})?$ constrains to a number from 0 to 100 with at most three decimal places. Multiply by 1000 and send the integer. "50" and "50.0" and "50.00" and "50.000" all send 50000; "12.345" sends 12345; "100" and "100.000" send 100000; "0" and "0.000" send 0. HOW THE TIE ACTUALLY WORKS, because the remedy below depends on it. The tie fact form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/box8DivisorTiesToMefString renders the NUMBER once, as AsDecimalString at scale 3, and compares that one rendering against the RAW String padded out four ways (String + ".000", + "00", + "0", and the String itself). It does not parse the String and it does not normalise it. HOW MANY LAWFUL SPELLINGS THERE ARE, and it is not four. The Match limit's integer part is [0-9]{1,2}, so it admits a leading zero: a one-digit percentage has EIGHT lawful spellings - "5", "5.0", "5.00", "5.000", "05", "05.0", "05.00", "05.000". The tie ties FOUR of them, the four without the leading zero, because those are the four the padding reaches. RESIDUE (a) OF THE REBODY CONTRACT IS DISCHARGED BY PROOF, AND NO BODY CHANGED. Residue (a) is a box 8 percentage on a form carrying NO box 9a percentage. The contract offered two discharges: a printed rule for the box-8-only share, or PROOF that the combination cannot arise on a correctly prepared form. The second is available on disk IN ITS WEAKER AND SUFFICIENT FORM and is re-derived here; this unit therefore changes no Derived body anywhere in either module, and that is the finding, not a shortfall.
THE STRONG CLAIM IS FALSE AND THE WEAK ONE IS WHAT THE GUARD NEEDS, corrected at the adversarial review before this append ever landed and stated first so no later reader rebuilds the overreach. A box 8 percentage beside a BLANK box 9a CAN appear on a correctly prepared form: box 9a's own carve-outs excuse it "for any IRA distributions or for a direct rollover" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), the box 8 percentage instruction at lines 1097-1100 carries no matching carve-out, and a partly-direct-rolled distribution is reported on SEPARATE Forms 1099-R for each part (lines 1105-1107), so the direct-rollover form is its own correctly prepared document. WHAT IS TRUE, and it is sufficient: such a form is never in the population this guard reaches. The guard only reaches a form on which the filer elects Form 4972 Part III - ../form4972TenYearElectionMade is a PER-FORM fact and the first arm of ../box8PercentageEntryConsistent frees every non-electing form outright - and every distribution box 9a excuses is barred from that election by Form 4972's own "Distributions That Don't Qualify" list. THE PROOF, in five printed steps, every one of them quoted on the authority comment of form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/box8MrdGrossUpApplies where the conjunct it licenses lives. (1) The box 8 percentage is entered ONLY for a multiple recipient lump-sum distribution (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16, RIGHT column). (2) A lump-sum distribution is "the distribution or payment in 1 tax year of a plan participant's entire balance from all of an employer's qualified plans of one kind" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 2), which is the same event box 2b calls a total distribution, "one or more distributions within 1 tax year in which the entire balance of the account is distributed" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 13) - the same event, not the same words. (3) Box 9a is entered whenever "this is a total distribution and it is made to more than one person" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), and (1)+(2) satisfy both halves of that condition exactly - "multiple recipient" IS "made to more than one person". (4) Box 9a's only carve-outs are "any IRA distributions or ... a direct rollover" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), and NEITHER can be the population where line 11 matters: "A distribution from an IRA" is itself an item of Form 4972's "Distributions That Don't Qualify for the 20% Capital Gain Election or the 10-Year Tax Option" list (f4972 lines 150-158 for the heading, line 82 for the bullet), and a rollover fails the same list from both sides - partially rolled over, "The part of a distribution not rolled over ... doesn't qualify" (f4972 lines 160-162), and wholly directly rolled over, no ordinary income part remains for the box 8 value, which the form confines to "figure tax on the ordinary income part of the distribution" (f4972 lines 74-78). (5) INDEPENDENTLY OF ALL FOUR: the printed procedure has no arm that divides line 11 without dividing line 8. The box 8 bullet is the THIRD bullet of Step 2, reached only after the two bullets that divide box 2a by the box 9a percentage (f4972 lines 192-197 and 206-210); Step 3 repeats the same pairing for the NUA election (lines 174-197 RIGHT column with the same box 8 bullet at 206-209); and Step 5 multiplies the result back by the box 9a percentage (lines 205-213 RIGHT column). Fact.Name: Total specified foreign financial assets are above the Form 8938 reporting threshold
Fact.Description:
Whether the TOTAL value of every specified foreign financial asset you hold is above the Form 8938 reporting threshold that applies to you. Asked only when a Form 1099-R carries a checked box 12.
THE THRESHOLD THAT APPLIES TO YOU is one of six printed pairs, and you satisfy it if EITHER figure is exceeded — the total on the LAST DAY of the tax year, or the maximum total AT ANY TIME during the tax year. Living IN the United States: unmarried, more than $50,000 / $75,000; married filing jointly, more than $100,000 / $150,000; married filing separately, more than $50,000 / $75,000. Living ABROAD — a tax home in a foreign country plus one of the presence-abroad tests: unmarried, more than $200,000 / $300,000; married filing jointly, more than $400,000 / $600,000; married filing separately, more than $200,000 on the last day of the tax year or more than $300,000 at any time during the tax year (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8938.pdf page 4: the sentence runs from the foot of the MIDDLE column, "$200,000 on the last day of the tax", to the head of the RIGHT column, "year or more than $300,000 at any" / "time during the tax year."; carried as a ledger parameter on form8938:/form8938ThresholdAtAnyTimeDuringYear).
THIS WRITABLE IS NOW THE FALLBACK, NOT THE ONLY ANSWER: form8938 carries the two asset aggregates and the residence fork, computes the threshold test from them when they are answered, and reads this attestation only when they are not (the writable-prefers idiom of form7206 line 2). A return that answered this question resolves exactly as before.
WHY THIS IS A SINGLE TAXPAYER STATEMENT rather than a computation, stated so the gap is named and not silently absorbed. Three inputs decide it and this dictionary holds only one. (a) The TOTAL VALUE of every specified foreign financial asset — a taxpayer-level aggregate that no information return supplies and this dictionary does not collect; a Form 1099-R box 12 speaks for ONE account. (b) The RESIDENCE test, which is a fork and not a refinement: the two sets of pairs differ by a factor of four, and reaching the abroad set needs a tax home in a foreign country plus either bona fide residence for an uninterrupted period that includes an entire tax year or presence in a foreign country for at least 330 full days in a 12-month period ending in the tax year — neither of which this dictionary collects. (c) The FILING STATUS, which this dictionary does hold, and which alone is not enough to pick a pair. So the honest first shape is the one the filer answers.
ANSWERING YES DOES NOT MEAN THE RETURN IS WRONG; it means a Form 8938 has to accompany it, and this dictionary does not produce Form 8938. That return is still refused, and the refusal now names the reason instead of refusing everyone whose payer checked a box. Leaving it UNANSWERED is also a refusal, and permanently the correct one: the threshold test has no safe default and no answer can be inferred from the form.

What is FREED is the filer with a checked box 12 whose total specified foreign financial assets are BELOW the threshold that applies to them — the common case, since the lowest of the six printed pairs starts at $50,000 and one Form 1099-R account says nothing about the total.

Fact.Name: Eligible retired public safety officer, from a plan that qualifies (IRC 402(l)(4))
Fact.Description:
Whether the recipient of this distribution is an ELIGIBLE RETIRED PUBLIC SAFETY OFFICER and this distribution came from an ELIGIBLE RETIREMENT PLAN.
NOT A BOX ON THE FORM, and the Description used to say "Box 7" until a review amendment corrected it. Box 7 of Form 1099-R is the distribution code; there is no public safety officer field on the form at all. This is a pure taxpayer attestation, which is also why IRC 402(l)(5)(A)(ii) makes the filer's own statement the substantiation.
ONE QUESTION CARRYING TWO STATUTORY TESTS, named here rather than one and two facts downstream, because this is the question the filer actually answers and it is load-bearing for a COMPUTATION rather than only for a knockout: (a) 402(l)(4)(B) - the person is a law enforcement officer, firefighter, chaplain, or member of a rescue squad or ambulance crew who is separated from service BY REASON OF DISABILITY OR ATTAINMENT OF NORMAL RETIREMENT AGE, from the employer who maintains the plan the distribution came from; and (b) 402(l)(4)(A) - that plan is a GOVERNMENTAL plan within the meaning of section 414(d) and is one of the four types described in clauses (iii) to (vi) of section 402(c)(8)(B): a qualified trust, a 403(a) plan, a 403(b) annuity, or a governmental 457(b) plan.
Neither test is separately modeled, and neither is silenced: the divergence is disclosed again on ../psoExcludableAmount. What the graph DOES enforce mechanically is the consequence of (b) that it can see: ../isSupportedPsoExclusion carries an explicit ../notIraSepSimple conjunct, so an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE distribution is kept out by the statutory test itself, and an IRA is none of the four types.
THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE NAMED THE WRONG MECHANISM AND IS KEPT VERBATIM, because the correction is only checkable against it. It read: "What the graph DOES enforce mechanically is the consequence of (b) that it can see - ../isSupportedPsoExclusion requires the form to be a line 5b pension, which keeps an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE distribution out, and an IRA is none of the four types." That stopped being true when a widening gave ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension an form1099RFrontier:../indirectRolloverInputsComplete disjunct whose only IRA gate is Any(../notIraSepSimple, a satisfied one-rollover-per-year answer) - so an IRA-flagged form with a completed 60-day rollover WAS a line 5b pension and drew the exclusion anyway. Being a line 5b pension has not carried the IRA test since. A later fill restored it as a conjunct of its own.

Fact.Name: Qualified health insurance premiums paid out of this distribution (IRC 402(l))
Fact.Description:
The amount of qualified health insurance premiums - accident or health plan, or a qualified long-term care insurance contract, covering the officer, spouse or dependents - that this distribution was used to pay. Asked only when ../hasPublicSafetyOfficerPremiums is true, and read only through ../psoPremiumsPaid, which defaults it to $0.
THE FILER'S OWN FIGURE, and it has to be: the premium is paid to an insurer, not reported in any box of the Form 1099-R, and IRC 402(l)(5)(A)(ii) makes the taxpayer's own ATTESTATION the substantiation when the distribution was paid to the officer rather than to the provider. There is nothing on the return to derive it from.
UNANSWERED IS NOT $0 FOR THE GUARD. ../psoPremiumsPaid defaults to $0 so that nothing downstream goes Incomplete, but ../isSupportedPsoExclusion requires this writable to be Complete, so a filer who attested to the premiums and never gave the amount is still REFUSED rather than silently excluded at $0.
