Fact.Name: The premiums figure as this fill reads it (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writablePsoPremiumsPaid when the filer answered the PSO premiums question YES and gave an amount, else $0. Complete-safe by construction: every arm resolves, so no consumer of the per-filer totals can be dragged Incomplete by an unanswered premium.

Fact.Name: This form has nothing includible for the PSO exclusion to reduce, so the exclusion is $0
Fact.Description:
THE ZERO-LINE CELL. A form that contributes NOTHING to Form 1040 line 5b, and for which IRC 402(l)(3)(A) therefore answers the exclusion at $0 rather than leaving it unanswered: "An amount shall be treated as a distribution for purposes of paragraph (1) only to the extent that such amount would be includible in gross income without regard to paragraph (1)." Where the includible amount is $0 the exclusion is $0 AND THE RETURN STILL FILES; refusing it refuses a case the statute computes.
The measure is form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount, which is exactly what this form puts on line 5b once every worksheet and election this module supports has run - the same quantity ../psoExcludableAmount already uses as its ceiling. So on this cell that ceiling returns LesserOf(premiums, $0) = $0 by arithmetic, with no special case anywhere.
THE FORM 4972 CONJUNCT IS A FENCE, NOT A TIDY-UP. A lump-sum distribution taxed on Form 4972 also has an ../effectiveTaxableAmount of $0 - that fact's FIRST Case says so - but its $0 is not "nothing was includible", it is "the includible amount is taxed on a separate schedule". IRC 402(l)(3)(A) may well license an exclusion there, and this dictionary has no line to put it on; that reading needs the Instructions for Form 4972, WHICH ARE NOT VENDORED (sources/ carries the FORM, f4972-ty2025-2025-11.txt, and no instructions file at all). Excluding the shape here keeps it refused rather than silently answered at $0. It is the one case /flowKnockoutRetirementPublicSafetyOfficer still refuses. (That rebody contract retired into a correct-refusal row in scripts/test_refusal_successor_allowlist.tsv; a retirement comment stands in its place in the records file.)
Both conjuncts are complete-safe: form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount and form1099RFrontier:../form4972InputsComplete each resolve on every form.
NARROWED, THOUGH. The FORM-4972-CONJUNCT paragraph above is kept verbatim and TWO of its claims are now known false.
(1) THE INSTRUCTIONS FOR FORM 4972 WERE ALWAYS ON DISK. There is no i4972 document to vendor: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4972.pdf returns HTTP 404, because the instructions are PRINTED ON THE FORM - https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, "General Instructions" at line 76 and "Specific Instructions" at line 221. The paragraph above checked for a FILE and not for its module's record.
(2) THE READING SPLITS THE SHAPE, AND ONLY HALF OF IT WAS EVER A REFUSAL. Form 4972's own "How To Report the Distribution", page 2 RIGHT column, item 3, reassembled from https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 2 (a three-column extraction; the sentence breaks across four printed lines and is quoted here as reassembled): "3. If you use Part III of Form 4972, don’t include any part of the distribution on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, lines 5a and 5b; or on Form 1041, line 8." A Part III form therefore puts NOTHING on line 5b, nothing is includible, IRC 402(l)(3)(A) answers its exclusion at $0, and THE RETURN FILES - the identical reasoning this cell already ships for shape (ii). The first conjunct is now Any(Not(form4972InputsComplete), form4972TenYearElectionMade); both disjuncts are complete-safe, and form4972TenYearElectionMade is TRUE whenever Part III is used, whether or not Part II is used with it, which is exactly the population item 3 governs.
WHAT IS STILL FENCED IS THE PART-II-ONLY ELECTION, and it is now a NAMED GAP rather than an unread document. Same instructions, same column, item 2, reassembled from lines 78-86: "2. If you don’t use Part III of Form 4972, but use Part II, report only the ordinary income portion of the distribution on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, lines 5a and 5b; or on Form 1041, line 8. The ordinary income portion is the amount from box 2a of Form 1099-R, minus the amount from box 3 of that form." An amount IS includible there, so Pub. 575's statement of the exclusion's own condition is satisfied - https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p575.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column, reassembled across the "inclu-/ded" line break: "You can exclude from income the smaller of the amount of the insurance premiums or $3,000. You can make this election only for amounts that would otherwise be included in your income." BUT form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount's FIRST Case returns $0 for EVERY complete Form 4972 election, Part II included, so this dictionary has no line 5b figure for the exclusion to reduce, and Pub. 575's mechanism for it - lines 459-460, RIGHT column, across the "exclu-/ded" break: "If you make this election, reduce the otherwise taxable amount of your pension or annuity by the amount excluded." - has nothing to operate on. That is a defect in effectiveTaxableAmount, not in this cell, and it understates line 5b on EVERY Part-II-only Form 4972 return, PSO or not. NAMED SUCCESSOR: form1099r-form4972-part2-ordinary-income-to-line5b.
THE PART-II-ONLY SUB-SHAPE IS NO LONGER FENCED - AND THIS FACT DID NOT CHANGE. Everything above is kept verbatim and the NAMED GAP it ends on is DISCHARGED. The sentence "form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount's FIRST Case returns $0 for EVERY complete Form 4972 election, Part II included" IS NO LONGER TRUE: that fact's Form 4972 Case is now split three ways, and a Part-II-only election resolves box 2a minus box 3 (Form 4972 page 2 RIGHT column item 2, lines 78-86).
THIS CELL IS UNCHANGED AND STAYS FALSE ON THAT SHAPE, correctly: a Part-II-only form with a positive ordinary income portion is not a form with nothing includible, so IRC 402(l)(3)(A) does not answer its exclusion at $0. The exclusion reaches it through the OTHER disjunct of conjunct (c) instead - ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension, whose first conjunct was narrowed the same day - and ../psoExcludableAmount's ceiling then does the arithmetic Pub. 575 lines 459-460 RIGHT column describe.

Fact.Name: This form's PSO premium exclusion is one this dictionary computes
Fact.Description:
The gate that decides whether the refusal lifts for this form. Every conjunct is a condition the printed rule states, and each one that fails leaves the knockout firing rather than producing a number.
(a) the filer answered the PSO premiums question YES (../hasPublicSafetyOfficerPremiums), which is the election IRC 402(l)(1) requires and is the only thing that puts this form in scope at all; (b) an AMOUNT is on the return (../writablePsoPremiumsPaid Complete). Without it the "smaller of the premiums or $3,000" has one of its two operands missing, and $0 is not a safe stand-in for a missing operand - it would silently file the pre-exclusion figure while the filer believed they had claimed the exclusion; (c) the form either reaches Form 1040 line 5b (../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension) OR has nothing includible for the exclusion to reduce (../psoZeroIncludibleAmountCell), in which case the exclusion is $0 and the return files; (d) the form is NOT an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE one (../notIraSepSimple). IRC 402(l)(4)(A) confines the exclusion to a GOVERNMENTAL plan described in section 402(c)(8)(B) clauses (iii)-(vi) - a qualified trust, a 403(a) plan, a 403(b) annuity or a governmental 457(b) plan - and an IRA is none of them. This is a CORRECT REFUSAL and it is PERMANENT: no successor is owed, because the statute answers it.
CONJUNCT (d) IS NEW AND THE SENTENCE IT REPLACES IS KEPT, because the change is only checkable against it. Conjunct (c) used to carry the IRA test too, and here is the whole of what it said, verbatim and unelided: "This is what keeps an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE form out: the exclusion is a line 5b reduction, and an IRA distribution lands on line 4b, so honouring an election there would subtract from a line the distribution never entered. It is also substantively right - IRC 402(l)(4)(A) confines the exclusion to a GOVERNMENTAL plan described in section 402(c)(8)(B) clauses (iii)-(vi), which is a qualified trust, a 403(a) plan, a 403(b) annuity or a governmental 457(b) plan, and an IRA is none of them. The same conjunct also excludes a box 2b "taxable amount not determined" form and an indirect rollover, both of which are refused elsewhere for their own reasons." BOTH HALVES OF THAT HAD STOPPED BEING TRUE. A widening of ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension gave it an ../indirectRolloverInputsComplete disjunct with no non-IRA gate, so an IRA-flagged form with a completed 60-day rollover satisfied (c) and drew an exclusion on a plan 402(l)(4)(A) excludes. The same widening admitted a box 2b form (through ../simplifiedMethodInputsComplete) and a non-IRA indirect rollover, which is CORRECT - each now has a Form 1040 line 5b amount of its own - so (c) is no longer the thing that excludes them, and this unit's ceiling swap on ../psoExcludableAmount is what makes the exclusion land on the right figure there. The statutory IRA test now stands on its own conjunct, where a later widening of (c) cannot silently take it away again.
CONJUNCT (c) WAS WIDENED, and the sentence it replaces is kept verbatim because the widening is only checkable against it: "(c) the form is one whose taxable amount reaches Form 1040 line 5b at all (../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension). The exclusion is a line 5b REDUCTION, so a form contributing nothing to that line gives it nowhere to sit;". THE SECOND SENTENCE OF THAT IS THE MISTAKE. A form contributing nothing to line 5b does not need the exclusion to sit anywhere: IRC 402(l)(3)(A) makes the exclusion $0 on it, and $0 is an ANSWER. Refusing the form refused a case the statute computes, which is the arm-4 residual the rebody contract at /flowKnockoutRetirementPublicSafetyOfficer named as owed. ../psoZeroIncludibleAmountCell is that cell, minus the Form 4972 shape it fences off for want of the (unvendored) Instructions for Form 4972.
RE-SCOPED, THOUGH. The two sentences above are kept verbatim and their Form 4972 clause no longer describes what (c) admits. The Instructions for Form 4972 are NOT unvendored - they are printed on the form, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 2 onward, and there is no i4972 document at all (HTTP 404). Read, they split the fenced shape: a PART III election keeps the whole distribution off Form 1040 lines 5a and 5b (line 88-91, RIGHT column), so ../psoZeroIncludibleAmountCell now admits it and (c) is satisfied through the cell; a PART-II-ONLY election reports box 2a minus box 3 ON lines 5a and 5b (lines 78-86, RIGHT column) but form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount returns $0 for it anyway, so the exclusion has no figure to reduce and (c) still fails there. The full reasoning and every quotation live on ../psoZeroIncludibleAmountCell's own Description.
WHAT IS NOT A CONJUNCT, AND WHY. The plan-type test itself (governmental vs private), the "separated by reason of disability or normal retirement age" test, and the "maintained by the employer you retired from" test are all carried by ../writeablePublicSafetyOfficer, the single YES/NO the interview asks. This dictionary does not decompose that question, and this fill does not pretend to: the divergence is disclosed on ../psoExcludableAmount rather than silently assumed away.
CONJUNCT (c) NOW ADMITS A PART-II-ONLY FORM 4972 FORM. This fact's BODY IS UNCHANGED. Everything above is kept unedited; one claim in it - that form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount returns $0 for a Form 4972 form anyway - is now true of a PART III election only. A Part-II-only election resolves box 2a minus box 3 and satisfies ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension, so conjunct (c)'s FIRST disjunct carries it and the exclusion is licensed exactly where Pub. 575 says it is: "You can make this election only for amounts that would otherwise be included in your income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p575.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column, reassembled across the "inclu-/ded" line break).

Fact.Name: What this form contributes to the officer's PSO exclusion, before the $3,000 cap
Fact.Description:
The smaller of the premiums paid out of this distribution and the amount this form actually puts on Form 1040 line 5b, or $0 when ../isSupportedPsoExclusion does not hold.
THE TAXABLE-AMOUNT CEILING IS IRC 402(l)(3)(A), NOT A DEFENSIVE CLAMP. "An amount shall be treated as a distribution for purposes of paragraph (1) only to the extent that such amount would be includible in gross income without regard to paragraph (1)" - Pub 575 says the same thing in return-preparation terms ("You can make this election only for amounts that would otherwise be included in your income"). A filer whose $8,000 of premiums came out of a distribution with $800 of taxable amount excludes $800, not $3,000.
THE CEILING IS form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount, NOT ../taxableAmount, and that swap is what this unit landed. ../taxableAmount is box 2a AS REPORTED, and it stopped being the includible figure the moment this module learned to compute one. On a box 2b "taxable amount not determined" form box 2a is unanswered, so ../taxableAmount is $0 and the ceiling excluded NOTHING on a form whose Simplified Method line 9 is $13,200 - a silently wrong number, not a refusal. On an indirect rollover the reported box 2a is the PRE-rollover figure, so the ceiling let the officer exclude against money that left the return with the rollover, and income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities subtracts with no floor. form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount is exactly what this form contributes to line 5b: /fullyTaxablePensions sums ../grossDistribution over the forms where gross EQUALS the effective taxable amount, /taxableAmountsOfPartiallyTaxablePensions sums the effective taxable amount over the rest, and every form satisfying ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension is in exactly one of the two. So the ceiling and the line the exclusion reduces are now the same quantity, per form. READ THAT PAIR'S OVER-THE-CEILING FORM WITH THE 402(l)(3)(B) GAP BELOW: its $200 answer stands on the PRINTED INSTRUCTIONS, not on 402(l)(3)(A) alone, because (3)(B) MODIFIES (A) and would let that form exclude the whole $201. The fixture pins what this dictionary ships and is correct as such; it is not a claim that $200 is the statutory answer.
WHY THE CAP IS NOT HERE. IRC 402(l)(2)'s $3,000 is a per-TAXPAYER annual ceiling, not a per-distribution one, so it is applied once per filer on /primaryFilerPsoExclusion and its twin. Applying it here as well would cap each form separately and let a two-form officer exclude $6,000.
DISCLOSED DIVERGENCE, per skeleton rule (9). Two conditions the statute states are carried by the single ../writeablePublicSafetyOfficer attestation and are NOT separately tested: that the plan is a GOVERNMENTAL plan of one of the four section 402(c)(8)(B) types (402(l)(4)(A)), and that the officer separated by reason of disability or attainment of normal retirement age from the employer maintaining that plan (402(l)(4)(B)).
AND TWO COORDINATION RULES, WHICH ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS EACH OTHER. Both say the excluded amount may not be counted twice; this dictionary carries them differently, so they are recorded as two gaps rather than one.
IRC 402(l)(7), "Coordination with medical expense deduction" - "The amounts excluded from gross income under paragraph (1) shall not be taken into account under section 213", which Pub 575 prints as "The amount excluded from your income can't be used to claim a medical expense deduction". NO CARRIER ANYWHERE. scheduleA:/writableMedicalExpenses is a bare filer-entered Schedule A line 1 total whose Description says nothing about this, so the graph cannot see whether the excluded premium is inside it. Named rather than guarded - a guard would have to refuse every itemiser who is also a retired public safety officer. THE ANCHOR ON THIS PARAGRAPH WAS WRONG UNTIL A REVIEW AMENDMENT CORRECTED IT: it read "IRC 402(l)(3)'s own closing rule". 402(l)(3) is "Distributions must otherwise be includible" and consists of (A) and (B) only; the bar is 402(l)(7). The substance was right and the citation pointed at the wrong clause, which is the one thing invariant #3 exists to stop.
IRC 402(l)(8), "Coordination with deduction for health insurance costs of self-employed individuals" - "The amounts excluded from gross income under paragraph (1) shall not be taken into account under section 162(l)". THIS ONE HAS A CARRIER, AND IT IS THE FILER'S ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN THE GRAPH'S, so it is a weaker gap than the 213 one and is recorded as such. Form 7206 line 1 prints the carve-out on the printed line ("Any amounts paid, not to exceed $3,000, from retirement plan distributions that were nontaxable because you are a retired public safety officer"), and this dictionary already relays it: the Description of scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid tells the filer to answer "excluding up to $3,000 of nontaxable retired public safety officer distributions". So the rule is disclosed where the filer meets it and is not silenced - but NOTHING CHECKS IT, because that writable is a total with no decomposition, exactly the 213 shape one paragraph up. What is new is that the figure the carve-out names is now COMPUTED: /psoPremiumExclusion is precisely "the nontaxable PSO distributions, not to exceed $3,000", so a successor can cross-check the two for the first time. Not done here, because doing it means either refusing a lawful combination or silently reducing a figure the filer entered, and this unit is not the place to choose between those.
AND IRC 402(l)(3)(B), "Application of section 72", ADDED BY A REVIEW ROUND - the one gap on this fact that is not a divergence or a coordination rule but a LIMIT ON THE CEILING THIS FACT COMPUTES. Notwithstanding section 72, the amounts distributed in the year (up to the paragraph (1) exclusion) are TREATED AS INCLUDIBLE up to what would have been includible if the officer's whole balance in the employer's eligible plans had been paid out that year, those plans taken as one contract. The "1 contract" clause is inside that HYPOTHETICAL; the rule itself binds a SINGLE plan and a SINGLE Form 1099-R, and it SHIFTS BASIS RECOVERY so the exclusion may reach the untaxed part of the balance rather than stopping at this year's section 72 taxable part. So it binds ANY Simplified Method form whose premiums exceed that year's includible part - it is NOT the employer-aggregation rule that is 402(l)(5)(B). THIS FACT DOES NOT IMPLEMENT IT AND CANNOT: nothing in this graph names the officer's balance, and ../simplifiedMethodInputsComplete's intake carries only this contract's investment, expected payments, prior recovery and payments received, so the (3)(B) amount is INDETERMINATE FROM COLLECTED INPUTS. What ships - the smaller of the premiums, this form's own includible amount and $3,000 - is what the 2025 Form 1040 instructions and Pub. 575 direct in as many words, and it UNDER-EXCLUDES relative to (3)(B) and can never over-exclude, because (3)(B) can only raise the includible ceiling and never lower it. NAMED, NOT GUARDED, and NOT an arm of /flowKnockoutRetirementPublicSafetyOfficer: the return computes and files, so a guard here would refuse every retired public safety officer with unrecovered cost. A successor owes an untaxed-balance intake first.
All five are named gaps. THE COUNT USED TO READ "All four", before a review round added the 402(l)(3)(B) gap above; the prior number is noted rather than silently overwritten.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's PSO-excludable total before the $3,000 ceiling
Fact.Description:
The aggregate IRC 402(l)(2)'s ceiling applies to, for the primary filer. The ceiling is PER TAXPAYER - 402(l)(1) speaks of "such employee" and 402(l)(2) of "the taxable year", so two spouses each retired as public safety officers have $3,000 apiece - which is why this is summed over /primaryFiler1099Rs rather than over the whole collection. Same shape, and the same reason, as /primaryFilerQcdTotal.
GUARDED with the IsComplete + CollectionSize pair the module's other per-filer sums use, so a return with no Form 1099-R at all resolves Complete $0 rather than Incomplete.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's PSO-excludable total before the $3,000 ceiling
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own aggregate, the sibling of /primaryFilerPsoExcludableTotal and identical in shape. It exists because the ceiling is per taxpayer: a joint return on which both spouses are retired public safety officers carries two $3,000 ceilings, and a single sum over the whole collection would give the couple one.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's PSO exclusion (IRC 402(l), capped at $3,000)
Fact.Description:
The smaller of the primary filer's excludable total and the $3,000 annual ceiling. This is the printed "smaller of the amount of the insurance premiums or $3,000" with the 402(l)(3)(A) includibility ceiling already applied per form inside the total.
AN ORDINARY CAP, NOT A REFUSAL, and that is a deliberate departure from the QCD ceiling one screen up. /form1099Rs/*/isQcdWithinAnnualCeiling REFUSES above its ceiling because nothing printed says which of two forms' exclusions is cut when they jointly exceed it. Here the allocation question never arises: the exclusion's only consumer is a single Form 1040 line 5b total, so the cut is taken once on the filer's aggregate and no per-form apportionment is needed to reach the printed number. The sources also answer the over-cap case outright - "you can still exclude from income only the smaller of the amount of the premiums paid or $3,000. The rest of the distribution is taxable to you and must be reported on line 5b" - so refusing there would refuse a case the instruction computes.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's PSO exclusion (IRC 402(l), capped at $3,000)
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own capped exclusion, the sibling of /primaryFilerPsoExclusion. The two are separate code rather than one shared expression for the same reason the QCD ceiling pair is: a shared ceiling would pass a primary-only test and silently give a two-officer couple one $3,000 between them.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 5b - the total retired-public-safety-officer premium exclusion
Fact.Description:
The two filers' capped exclusions added. This is the term income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities subtracts, and it exists as a return-level fact for the same reason /form1099Rs/*/line4bTaxableAmount exists on the line 4b side: line 5b is summed in ANOTHER module out of two collection sums of box 1 and box 2a, and an exclusion computed here could not reach the line without a summand of its own.
NEVER OVER-SUBTRACTS - though it once could have. Each per-form term is bounded by that form's own form1099RFrontier:../effectiveTaxableAmount, which is precisely what the form contributes to line 5b: /fullyTaxablePensions sums ../grossDistribution over the forms whose gross EQUALS their effective taxable amount, and /taxableAmountsOfPartiallyTaxablePensions sums the effective taxable amount over the rest, so a form satisfying ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension is in exactly one of the two and its term is already inside the total it reduces. The sum of the terms is therefore at or below the sum it is subtracted from, and the per-filer $3,000 caps only lower it further. Line 5b cannot go negative through this fact.
THE PRIOR VERSION OF THAT PARAGRAPH WAS FALSE, and it is corrected rather than deleted because a later reader would otherwise re-derive the same wrong reason. It read: "Each per-form term is bounded by that form's own ../taxableAmount and every form contributing one satisfies ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension, so the form's box 2a (or, for a fully taxable form, its equal box 1) is already inside the line 5b total this reduces." Box 2a as reported stopped being the form's contribution to line 5b when the module learned to compute an effective taxable amount: on an indirect rollover the reported box 2a is the PRE-rollover figure, so a $20,000 box 2a rolled over down to $2,000 admitted a $3,000 exclusion against a $2,000 line, and income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities has no floor under its Subtract. The ceiling swap on ../psoExcludableAmount is the fix.

Fact.Name: This fully taxable form carries a PSO exclusion, so its gross belongs on line 5a
Fact.Description:
True when the form is fully taxable (box 2a equals box 1) AND a positive PSO exclusion is computed on it. It exists only to feed /fullyTaxablePensionsWithPsoExclusionGross.
WHY LINE 5a NEEDS A TERM AT ALL. income:/pensionsAndAnnuities carries /taxFreePensionRollovers and /partlyTaxablePensions and nothing else, because a fully taxable pension has the same figure on both lines and the instruction lets line 5a stay blank. A PSO exclusion breaks that equality without touching box 2a, and the instruction is explicit about what then happens: "Report your total distributions on line 5a and the taxable amount on line 5b." So a fully taxable form with an exclusion acquires a line 5a it did not have. A PARTLY taxable form needs no term here - its gross is already on line 5a through /partlyTaxablePensions - which is why this predicate tests ../isFullyTaxable rather than ../isFullyOrPartlyTaxablePension, and why the two can never double-count the same form.

Whether the money on this Form 1099-R was a qualified disaster recovery distribution.
SCREEN SPEC. Question: "Was any of this distribution a qualified disaster recovery distribution?" Help text: a qualified disaster recovery distribution is one received on or after the first day of a qualified disaster's incident period and before the day that is 180 days after the applicable date for that disaster, by someone whose principal place of abode was in the qualified disaster area at some time during the incident period and who sustained an economic loss by reason of the disaster (IRC 72(t)(11)(A); 26 U.S.C. 72, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section72&num=0&edition=2024). The Instructions for Forms 1099-R and 5498 name no Form 1099-R box and no box 7 code for a qualified disaster distribution; the only disaster BOXES they describe are the Form 5498 boxes 14a and 14b, and those report a REPAYMENT (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 24). So this is the filer's own statement about the distribution, not a figure copied off the payer's form.
ASKED-WHEN: on EVERY Form 1099-R, whatever box 7 holds. The definition turns on the disaster and on the recipient, never on a distribution code, and the Form 8915-F instructions contemplate one received as a beneficiary — the case a payer codes 4 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8915f.pdf, page 6).
VALIDATION: yes or no. UNANSWERED POSTURE: this answer and the derived ../qualifiedDisasterDistribution stay Incomplete, and an Incomplete form is not counted by the refusal — the return files with box 2a taxed in full, which is the amount owed if no disaster treatment is claimed. WHAT IT FEEDS: a yes refuses the return through /flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedDisasterDistribution, because the year's income inclusion and any repayment belong on Form 8915-F and nothing in this collection carries them.

Whether this Form 1099-R reports a qualified disaster recovery distribution, as the filer answered. It is the filer's answer on every form, whatever box 7 holds: IRC 72(t)(11)(A) makes the distribution qualify on the disaster's incident period and the recipient's principal place of abode, so no distribution code can put a form in or out of the class. Incomplete while the question is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Knockout when a Form 1099-R reports a qualified disaster recovery distribution
Fact.Description: Refuses a return on which any Form 1099-R answers the qualified disaster recovery distribution question yes. Such a distribution is not taxed the way box 2a is: unless the recipient elects otherwise, the amount that must be included in gross income is included ratably over three tax years, and a contribution made back to an eligible retirement plan within three years of the distribution undoes it. Both are Form 8915-F computations keyed to a disaster rather than to a payer's form, and nothing here ties one Form 1099-R to the Form 8915-F line that carries it, so a return that filed on box 2a alone would report this year's income wrongly and would double count against any Form 8915-F instalment the return already carries. Counts only the forms that answer the question true; a form whose answer is unanswered is not counted.

ASK: "Does a Form 5329 exception to the 10% additional tax apply to this distribution?" HELP: box 7 says the payer knows of no exception, but the taxpayer may still qualify - the exceptions are listed by number in the 2025 Instructions for Form 5329, Line 2. ASKED WHEN: ../flowQualifiedEarlyDistribution is true, i.e. box 7 is one of the printed early-distribution codes (1, J, S and their permitted pairs, and 1D for a nonqualified annuity, whose exceptions are the section 72(q)(2) list Pub. 575 gives). UNANSWERED: the graph claims no exception for this form - the additional tax applies to its whole includible amount, never less - and ../isComplete reports the form incomplete under the same gate. No dictionary fact reads ../isComplete: it is the completeness signal an application screen gates on, so holding the return until the question is answered is the application's gate, not a refusal the graph makes. VALIDATION: yes/no. FEEDS: ../causesQualifiedEarlyDistributionKO, and through it /flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedEarlyDistribution, which refuses the return only when the answer is yes AND form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount is left unanswered AND this item's recipient was NOT 59½ on every day of the tax year (../filerAge59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear) - answering the exception AMOUNT there is what lets the return file for every other recipient. When this item's recipient was 59½ on every day of the tax year, exception 12 is applied by the graph without this answer and without an amount (form5329:/form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount or its secondary twin), so the return files either way — answer yes only for another exception, whose amount is netted out before the derived exception 12 amount so it is never excepted twice.

TRUE when box 7 puts this Form 1099-R in the population Form 5329 Part I line 1 taxes: the printed early-distribution codes, and only those. Code 1 (early distribution, no known exception) and the pairs the payer may use with it that do not change what the money is - 1B, 1K, 1L, 1M and their reverses; code J (early distribution from a Roth IRA, no known exception); code S (early distribution from a SIMPLE IRA in the first 2 years) and the JS pair, in both orders, because ../distributionCode is the payer's characters upper-cased and stripped in payer order. The 8- and P-paired codes are OUT, and that exclusion is TAX-NEUTRAL rather than a statement that the money never belongs on Form 5329. A 401(k) or 403(b) excess deferral or excess aggregate contribution is excluded by the Part I instruction outright. But the earnings on an IRA excess contribution returned under section 408(d)(4) are put ON line 1 by the Line 1 instruction ("A qualified retirement plan including earnings on withdrawn" / "excess contributions to your IRAs included in income in", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5329.pdf, page 3) and excepted on line 2 by the Line 15 instruction ("the year in which you report the earnings. Report this" / "amount on line 2 and enter exception number 21.", lines 436-437). Line 1 and line 2 net to $0, so leaving the item out computes the same tax; what it does not do is print those two lines and exception number 21. Code 1D (and D1) is IN: code D marks a distribution from a nonqualified annuity, and paired with code 1 it is an early distribution with no known exception. Section 72(q)(1) increases the tax by 10 percent of the includible portion of any amount received under an annuity contract, and Pub. 575 puts that tax on Form 5329 with the qualified-plan tax: most distributions from qualified retirement plans and nonqualified annuity contracts made before age 59 1/2 are subject to it, and a filer who must pay it reports it on Form 5329. The section 72(q)(2) exceptions are not section 72(t)(2)'s - they include investment in the contract before August 14, 1982 (Form 5329 exception 16) and the immediate-annuity and qualified-funding-asset cases Pub. 575 lists - so for a code D form the filer's exception answer (../writableQualifiedEarlyDistribution and its amount) is measured against that list. The age exception is the same in both subsections, so the age 59 1/2 exception form5329 derives from the date of birth applies to a code D form as well.

Fact.Name: This form's recipient was 59 1/2 on every day of the tax year
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the date of birth of THIS FORM'S recipient (../filer) is on or before July 1, 1965. Age 59 1/2 falls on the date six calendar months after the 59th anniversary of birth, so a filer born July 1, 1965 reached it on January 1, 2025 and every earlier birth date reached it sooner: such a recipient was 59 1/2 or older on every day of 2025, so every distribution they received in 2025 was made on or after the date they attained 59 1/2 and is excepted from the additional tax under IRC 72(t)(2)(A)(i), whatever box 7 says. FALSE, never Incomplete, when the recipient's date of birth is unanswered, when this form has no recipient link, and for any later birth date: the IsComplete leg is tested first, so this fact is Complete on every return and can never be a placeholder. Read by /flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedEarlyDistribution, which does not refuse a recipient in this band for leaving the per-item exception amount blank, because the whole line 2 amount of such an item is derived without it (form5329:/form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount and its secondary twin).
THE SAME BAND EDGE IS COMPUTED PER FILER IN form5329, at /form5329PrimaryFilerAge59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear and its secondary twin, from the same July 1, 1965 literal. The duplication is a MODULE-DIRECTION consequence, not a choice: form5329 reads form1099Rs, so form1099Rs cannot read form5329, and this fact is a PER-ITEM join on the item's own recipient rather than a per-filer return-level Boolean. The single home for the band edge is filers:/filers/*/age59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear, which both modules would then read; that fact does not exist yet.

Fact.Name: Form 1040 line 5c box 2, the retired public safety officer box, derived from the exclusion
Fact.Description: Whether Form 1040 line 5c box 2 is checked, computed as GreaterThan(/psoPremiumExclusion, $0) rather than asked. The printed box is not an independent question: it is the ANNOUNCEMENT of the section 402(l) exclusion this module already computes and already subtracts. /psoPremiumExclusion sums the two filers' capped exclusions and is read by income:/taxablePensionsAndAnnuities, so a return either took the exclusion or did not, and the box must say which. Until this fact existed the box was the separate attestation /writableLine5cPsoBoxChecked, so a filer could take the exclusion with the box unchecked, or check the box with no exclusion, and nothing in the graph noticed. ALWAYS COMPLETE: /psoPremiumExclusion is a sum of complete safe per filer terms, so this Bool resolves on every return, False on the overwhelming majority that claim no exclusion. THE ATTESTATION IS RETIRED and this fact is now the only answer for the box. The hand off the sentence this replaces asked for is done: dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040/en/configuration.yml line 154 maps c1_39[0] to /line5cPsoBoxChecked, leaving /writableLine5cPsoBoxChecked mapped by nothing and read by nothing, and this unit deleted it. THE RETIREMENT IS TOTAL, not a demotion behind a predicate: /psoPremiumExclusion is a sum of complete safe per filer terms and resolves on every return, so the computed arm is available on every supported return and there is no case in which the filer's own checkbox was the only source of the answer. The election itself is still the filer's: it is stated by the premium and eligibility intakes /psoPremiumExclusion reads, not by a second free standing checkbox that could contradict them.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 7 column B, this return's share of this payer's pension income
Fact.Description:
The share of ONE Form 1099-R's pension income that belongs on THIS separate return, which Form 8958 line 7 column B prints: column A less the crossing half. Column A of the row is ../communityAllocablePensionBase, this form's own contribution to Form 1040 line 5b, and column C is ../communityPropertyAllocatedPensionIncomeRounded, the half of the community portion that leaves this return. Subtracting one from the other leaves the whole of the separate part plus half of the community part, which is exactly what the form's operative sentence describes and exactly what the module's return level adjustment /communityPropertyPensionAllocationAdjustment already assumes. It also makes the columns foot by construction, B plus C equal to A, on every row.
WHY THIS IS A SUBTRACTION AND NOT A SWITCH, unlike the wages, interest and dividend rows of this class. Pension community character is a DOLLAR PORTION rather than a Boolean (../writableCommunityIncomePortion, clamped by ../communityIncomePortion), because Publication 555's Henry Wright example is a PARTLY community pension. A two arm switch on a Boolean cannot say half of 12,000 is community; the subtraction says it without inventing a ratio: 12,000 base less the 3,000 crossing half is 9,000 on this return, which is the Wright answer.
WHOLE DOLLARS, BECAUSE THIS MODULE ROUNDS AT THE FORM. Both terms are already whole dollar quantities in this module (../communityAllocablePensionBase is built from Round wrapped per form amounts and ../communityPropertyAllocatedPensionIncomeRounded is Round wrapped itself), so the difference carries no cents and the name does not claim otherwise. On an odd dollar community portion the half rounds away from zero and this column takes the residual dollar, the disclosed consequence the half's own Description already records.
OFF GATE AND ON A SEPARATE PROPERTY ROW THE WHOLE ITEM IS THIS RETURN'S: the crossing half is $0 on a return that is not an allocation return and $0 on a form whose community portion is $0, so column B equals column A and column C is $0, which is the ordinary separate return answer. On an IRA form and on a Form 4972 Part III form the base is $0 and all three columns are $0, which is the form's own IRA rule rather than a gap. A spouse's partly community pension never reaches a filable return: ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue and lifts a secondary filer's form out of the guard only when ../isWhollyCommunityIncome.
